body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chief electoral officers (CEOs) of several states and Union territories have shared no eligible voter will be left out of the electoral rolls, announcing special enrolment camps at polling stations, schools and colleges as part of a drive ordered by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

Adding to this, The drive follows ECI instructions issued on October 1 to enrol eligible electors who were left out. (Ishant Chauhan/HT) Revealed via CEOs’ official social media handles on Monday, this comes amid nationwide protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, In Rajasthan, 41 district election officers (DEOs) have started a “proactive campaign”, with camps being held at 61,404 booths, the state CEO shared. Chhattisgarh’s 33 DEOs have launched a similar drive across 27,196 booths, and camps are also being held in schools and colleges. Kerala shared camps are being held at village offices for all 30,471 booths across its 14 districts.
Notably, Similar announcements were made by CEOs of other states and UTs including Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana.

As per the latest buzz, In Odisha, camps are being organised at 45,250 polling booths across the state. In Ladakh, electors are being facilitated through 595 polling stations. The Lakshadweep administration shared special camps are being held across the Union territory. In Jharkhand, officials inspected special camps at polling stations in Bhojudih, among other places.

In further updates, The drive follows ECI instructions issued on October 1 to enrol eligible electors who were left out. In Chhattisgarh, the campaign began on October 8, with BLOs visiting homes, schools and colleges, and holding camps at booths.

On top of that, Voters with complaints have been asked to contact booth-level officers (BLOs), assistant electoral registration officers (AEROs), electoral registration officers (EROs) or DEOs. Rajasthan has listed 61,404 BLOs, 854 AEROs, 200 EROs and 41 DEOs for this. Kerala has 30,471 BLOs and 140 each of AEROs and AEROs. Lakshadweep has 64 BLOs, 10 AEROs, one ERO and one DEO.

Delhi’s CEO shared about 3.3 million entries in the capital’s voter list had been flagged under “logical discrepancy” or as un-mapped, and around 2 million of them have been resolved. It listed 14,947 BLOs, 902 AEROs, 70 EROs and 13 DEOs for grievances.

title: Ramesh Taurani recalls Alka Yagnik’s rise in the ’90s: “She was getting the most songs”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Discussing the music landscape of the period, Ramesh Taurani recalled that established voices such as Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle continued to be important choices for filmmakers, while a new generation of singers was gaining prominence.
Adding to this, “Back then, Lata Ji and Asha Ji were already established. When we used to make music, Lata Ji was our first preference, followed by Alka and Anuradha,” Taurani shared.

Meanwhile, He went on to recall the emergence of singers including Kumar Sanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan. According to him, films such as Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak , Aashiqui , Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante helped establish the new voices in the industry as their songs became popular with audiences.

Notably, “The idea was that in the ’90s, when new singers like Shanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan came in, these four made it big. Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak , Aashiqui , Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante were hits, and their songs became superhits,” he recalled.

As per the latest buzz, Taurani also drew a comparison between the newer singers and the established female playback voices of the previous generation. He recalled that Anuradha Paudwal was being viewed as a successor to Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik was increasingly being positioned as a voice comparable to Asha Bhosle.
In further updates, “The idea then was that Anuradha Paudwal was the new Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik became the new Asha Bhosle,” Taurani shared.

On top of that, According to Taurani, the shift in Anuradha Paudwal’s movie career eventually created more opportunities for Alka Yagnik. He recalled that after Paudwal stopped singing for films and became associated exclusively with T-Series, Alka began receiving a wider variety of female playback assignments.

“Luckily, Anuradha Ji stopped singing for films and made herself exclusive to T-Series. This worked in Alka Ji’s favour, as she got both Lata Ji and Asha Ji type songs, whether they were solos, duets or shayari,” he shared.

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 11: Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam: The Conclusion is showing no signs of slowing down at the ticket-window. The movie crossed the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark on its tenth day. It has also emerged as the biggest ticket-window success of Ajay's career, giving the star a new career high.

Adding to this, According to trade tracker Sacnilk, the crime thriller has collected over ₹ 313 crore rupees net in India in just 11 days, following another strong weekend in theatres. The movie coll ected ₹ 4.98 crore rupees net in India on Day 11, taking its total domestic collection to ₹ 313.98 crore rupees, according to live ticket-window tracking data. The movie recorded these numbers across 13,594 shows on Monday.

Meanwhile, The second weekend gave the movie another boost. After earning ₹ 14.50 crore rupees on its second Friday, Day 8, collections rose to ₹ 26.50 crore rupees on Saturday, Day 9, across 14,903 shows. The movie added another ₹ 22.50 crore rupees on Sunday, Day 10, from 14,872 shows. Although Sunday's collection was 15.1% lower than Saturday's, the movie still enjoyed a strong weekend and crossed the ₹ 300 crore rupees mark within ten days of rollout.

Notably, The movie's ticket-window run has taken Ajay Devgn past his previous career record. Drishyam 3 has overtaken Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior to become his highest-grossing movie so far. It is also the first Ajay-led movie to cross ₹ 300 crore rupees in India net collections.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Abhishek Pathak, Drishyam 3: The Conclusion features Ajay Devgn, Tabu, Jaideep Ahlawat, Shriya Saran and Prakash Raj. Rolled out in theatres on October 2, 2026, the movie brings the popular crime thriller franchise to its concluding chapter. Drishyam The Conclusion is backed by Star Studio18 and Panorama Studios, with Abhishek Pathak returning to direct the third instalment. He has also co-written the movie with Aamil Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh. Alok Jain, Ajit Andhare, Kumar Mangat Pathak and Abhishek Pathak are producing the movie.

On top of that, Speaking at FICCI Frames, Ajay shared, “The original one they did not have Akshay Khanna's character as such but 3 is a completely new script. They are two very different films. The way Abhishek and the writers have worked so hard on the script for the past maybe two years that it really really gives you a high. title: 'Mini-India', a space for all: Jantar Mantar's special place on Delhi's protest map
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Till the early 1990s, Jantar Mantar, an 18th century astronomical observatory built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur, was a part of the list of places to sightsee in Delhi , and school students were taken there for annual excursions. In fact, the Misra Yantra inside the Jantar Mantar observatory complex was the inspiration behind the logo of the Asian Games held in New Delhi in 1982.

Adding to this, But Jantar Mantar was not always associated with protesters and posters or barricades and banners. In fact, Boat Club lawns were the preferred protest site, and in 1988, farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait led the most significant protest there that lasted a week and saw lakhs of people. Five years later, protests and rallies were banned at Boat Club and the road abutting Jantar Mantar was notified as a designated protest site.

Meanwhile, Called “Mini India” by historian Ramchandra Guha , neem-lined Jantar Mantar is the site that people from across the country gather hoping to be heard. Guha in 'India After Gandhi' describes the transition in 1990s. He notes that Rajpath , where the grounds meant to be empty except on ceremonial days, had become a village of tents, each with colourful placards hung outside it. The people within these tents and the causes they upheld were ever changing. The hill peasants replaced by industrial workers; the Maharashtra farmers by Tibetan refugees; the Konkani speakers by Hindu monks demanding a ban on cow slaughter.

Notably, "In the early nineties, these tents were summarily dismantled by a government worried about the impression made on foreign visitors by such open expression of dissent. Rajpath was vacated of encroachments and the lawns restored to their former glory but the protesters regrouped, and relocated. They now placed themselves a mile to the north-west, next to the Jantar Mantar observatory in Connaught Place. Here they were away from the eyes of the state, but directly in view of the citizens who daily passed through this busy shopping district," Guha writes.

As per the latest buzz, For 33 years, the half a kilometer stretch near the observatory has provided space for all, measuring public discontent, bringing together farmers, workers, veterans, students, activists and citizens protesting against decisions they believed had left them unheard. On an average, the Parliament Street police station receives more than 24,000 requests for permission to hold protests every year. One could walk on this half a kilometer stretch on single street to get a glimpse of grievances across India.

In further updates, In 2017, Tamil Nadu farmers with mice in their hands or their mouths who wanted to draw attention of the government to the agrarian crisis reached Jantar Mantar. In same year, a man from Madhya Pradesh had spent years protesting against government documents declaring him dead and lived in Jantar Mantar. Eleven ex-servicemen recorded the over 700 days of their relay hunger strike for one-rank-one-pension to followers of Asaram Bapu and Rampal who had spent years camping on Mantar, trying to persuade the authorities to free their jailed gurus.

On top of that, The initial protests of the Anna Hazare movement started from Jantar Mantar in April 2011. Not to forget the annual Delhi Queer Pride parade. In 2105, retired Indian military and paramilitary personnel sat there and demanded fair implementation of One Rank One Pension (OROP), with subsequent demonstrations and re-gatherings taking place in 2016, 2019. Parents, relatives and friends of murdered Noida teen Arushi Talwar demanded justice at Jantar Mantar in 2011 and 2013. Even followers of jailed self-styled godmen; animal lovers against use of cow’s milk; dog haters; members of Akhil Bharatiya Joota Maaro Andolan; and a sole protester from Chandauli who believed satellites hacked into people’s brains in his hometown have found themselves at Jantar Mantar over the years.

On Monday, the Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated protest venue. An order issued by the Delhi Commissioner of Police Anurag Kumar states that based on recommendations of committee Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified. Three new venues-- Ramlila ground, Burari ground and CBD ground in East Delhi have been designated as new venues for protests and demonstrations.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Students continued their protest for the second consecutive day at the Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Ranchi, on Monday following the death by suicide of a first-year student on Saturday night.

Adding to this, The incident came to light on Saturday night when hostel residents alerted the institute administration after finding the student’s room locked from the inside. (X) The students accused the institute administration of negligence and failing to provide emergency medical facilities in the hostel. They demanded the immediate resignation of director Rajiv Srivastava.

Meanwhile, “In an attempt to defuse the tense situation, the institute’s chairperson arrived at the protest site to hold talks with the students. However, a standoff ensued before formal discussions could begin. The examinations, which began on October 8, could not be held on Monday due to the agitation,” IIT registrar Munuren Samson Champia shared.

Notably, The students have demanded accountability for the alleged institutional lapses that they claim delayed emergency medical care for the deceased student. They have also called for the director’s immediate resignation, the implementation of a robust, round-the-clock emergency medical system in the hostel premises, and the permanent deployment of a campus doctor and a dedicated ambulance to ensure a swift response to medical emergencies.
As per the latest buzz, Officer-in-charge of Khelgaon police station Nirbhay Kumar verified the students’ demands but declined to elaborate further.

In further updates, “The students are protesting peacefully, and no law and order problem has arisen so far. The students’ demands and their resolution by the institute’s management are internal matters. The police have no role in the matter,” Kumar shared.
On top of that, He added that a case of unnatural death had been registered and an investigation was underway to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.

The incident came to light on Saturday night when hostel residents alerted the institute administration after finding the student’s room locked from the inside. The administration subsequently informed the police.

It has also brought up a question that the makers will have to answer: why should audiences watch a remake when the original is already available?

Adding to this, Sunny Deol in Suryaa's first look whereas Joju George in Joseph. Sunny Deol unveils first look and rollout date The first look of Suryaa was unveiled on October 12 along with the rollout date. Sunny looks markedly different from his usual action-hero avatar in his first look motion poster. With a rugged appearance and an intense gaze, he hints at a man haunted by his past and struggling to confront truths he can no longer ignore. The tagline reads, “Torn between his past and present, he uncovers the truth”. The makers describe the protagonist as a man “drawn into a web of unanswered questions and buried truths,” whose investigation “soon takes him into territory far more complex than he anticipated”.

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram Interestingly, Suryaa is based on Joseph, the 2018 Malayalam movie starring Joju George as a retired police officer drawn into a murder investigation that forces him to confront his own past. With Joseph director M Padmakumar returning to helm the new version, the star gets a chance to step away from his familiar action-hero image and take on a character driven by grief, secrets and personal turmoil.

Notably, The announcement has not been met with excitement by everyone. On X, several users pointed out that Joseph is already available to watch, questioning whether the Hindi version offers enough reason for audiences to buy a theatre ticket. One user wrote: “For those who are unaware, #Suryaa is a remake of Malayalam movie Joseph. Anyone who wants to watch it, can watch it online & save your money on some original movie.”

As per the latest buzz, Another echoed the sentiment: “For those who are asking, #Suryaa starring #SunnyDeol is a REMAKE of Malayalam movie JOSEPH So my question is why would anyone watch it in Theatres if you can watch it ONLINE?” Many also pointed out that the movie will face immense threat at the ticket-window due to the Diwali rollout of Ramayana: Part 1, in which Sunny Deol is playing the role of Hanuman.

In further updates, Despite the criticism, some viewers are interested in seeing Deol in a crime thriller, particularly one that appears to move away from his usual action-heavy roles. One user offered a succinct summary: “Different look! Crime-thriller genre! A cop investigates a double homicide while the secrets from his own life gets revealed. If executed and promoted well, can be a success for #SunnyDeol.”

On top of that, Drishyam, Vikram Vedha and The Departed have all shown how stories can find audiences in different settings and languages. The real test is whether the adaptation respects what worked in the original while giving viewers a reason to experience it again.

When Joseph arrived in theatres in November 2018, few could have predicted just how far the movie would travel. Directed by M. Padmakumar and written by former police officer Shahi Kabir, the thriller was as per reports made on a budget of ₹ 3 crore rupees and went on to earn ₹ 28 crore rupees. It also completed a run of more than 100 days in theatres.

title: Sonali Bendre tells Madhuri Dixit why she chose to love her body during cancer battle despite immense pain
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sonali Bendre has been open about her battle with cancer and of late spoke about her approach to dealing with the disease. At the grand premiere of Kon Honar Crorepati, the Marathi version of Kaun Banega Crorepati hosted by Madhuri Dixit , the star reflected on how the experience changed her perspective on her body and life.

Adding to this, Sonali Bendre spoke about cancer battle on Kon Honar Crorepati. During the episode, Madhuri lauded Sonali for battling and overcoming cancer. Sonali, however, offered a different perspective, explaining that she had never chosen to look at the experience as a battle. Instead, she focused on understanding her body, treating it with love and learning from one of the most challenging phases of her life.

Meanwhile, Sharing her experience of dealing with cancer, Sonali shared, “I mean, you know, actually, we always say that someone has overcome cancer. But, all jokes apart, we say all these things while laughing and joking. But at that time, the actual intention was not to overcome it. It was to understand why this was happening and what I could learn from it. And trust me, I actually learnt a lot from it. And that is how I looked at it.”

Notably, Sonali shared that her approach to the disease involved changing how she viewed her body and the pain she was experiencing. She explained why the language of fighting or overcoming cancer felt negative to her.

As per the latest buzz, She shared, “Because I feel that when we say we have overcome something, it somehow feels like a fight. There is a sense of negativity somewhere. And, after all, it is our own body, isn’t it? The cancer cells are also our own cells. So, how can we fight ourselves? So how do I love my body the way it is? And I thought that maybe I should treat it with love. It’s very difficult to love something that was giving you so much pain. But I think that’s probably what worked for me. And that’s where it went.”

In further updates, Sonali was diagnosed with high-grade metastatic cancer in July 2018 and revealed the news publicly through a social media post. She subsequently travelled to New York for treatment and continued to share updates about her experience with followers. She also spoke about the physical and emotional challenges of the diagnosis in interviews. She achieved remission and was declared cancer-free in 2021.

On top of that, After overcoming cancer, Sonali made a comeback to acting. She has continued to explore different roles across films and television. She of late appeared in the web shows like Raakh and The Broken News. She also hosts reality game show Pati Patni Aur Panga with comedian Munawar Faruqui.

title: Delhi Police take down 300 social media posts in crackdown on ‘misinformation’ amid protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police is monitoring social media platforms to curb the spread of misinformation amid protests in the capital, with around 300 posts allegedly aimed at spreading rumours or creating public unrest taken down, police sources shared, according to PTI on Monday.

Adding to this, Delhi Police is monitoring various social media platforms to curb the spread of misinformation amid protests in the national capital (Sanjeev Verma/ Hindustan Times) The action comes amid heightened tensions following protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of police misconduct during the demonstrations. Police are scanning online platforms to identify fabricated videos, misleading claims and content that could potentially disturb public order.

Meanwhile, The police have also approached social media platform X, seeking the removal of objectionable and allegedly misleading content linked to the protests, according to PTI. Further action is being taken against posts found to be spreading misinformation or attempting to incite unrest, they added.

Notably, The crackdown on misleading content comes days after the arrest of a 24-year-old man, identified as Nadeem Ahmed, for allegedly using artificial intelligence (AI) tools to create and circulate a fabricated video depicting a police officer sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against the CEC.

As per the latest buzz, According to police, Ahmed allegedly circulated the video falsely portraying a police personnel in an objectionable manner. The case is being investigated separately from allegations of sexual harassment levelled against police personnel by women journalists.

In further updates, The development comes against the backdrop of protests organised by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar, where demonstrators demanded Kumar’s resignation over allegations of “vote chori”. Delhi Police had detained several protesters and key figures during the demonstrations, citing the lack of permission for the protest.

On top of that, The protests also triggered extensive security arrangements in central Delhi, with restrictions imposed around sensitive locations and metro services affected as authorities sought to prevent further disruption. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers to manage crowds and maintain order.

The demonstrations were also marked by allegations of violence and intimidation. Groups of men allegedly threatened and assaulted protesters and journalists in Connaught Place and near the MCD Civic Centre, even as security personnel were deployed across the city centre.

title: Actor and MP Ravi Kishan on playing Lord Ram in Ayodhya Ki Ramleela: Dara hua hoon, can't afford to go wrong with Shri Ram
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star and Parliamentarian Ravi Kishan , who will be essaying the role of Shri Ram at Ayodhya Ki Ramleela on October 19 and 20 in New Delhi, with the event being telecast worldwide, says he is "scared" to play the deity on stage.

Adding to this, Star Ravi Kishan and his AI image in role of Shri Ram that he will perform at Ayodhya Ki Ram Leela in New Delhi on October 19 and 20 (Photo: Instagram and AI) He tells HT City, “Pehli baar Shri Ram ke roop dharan karne ka saubhagya mila and I pray and wish that He enters my body and gives me the energy to perform with grace. I have earlier played Parashuram and Kevat, as a kid I have played Mata Sita as well, and in a TV serial I have essayed the role of Shri Krishna as well, but this is different. I always want to play Shri Ram”

Meanwhile, Admitting that he is feeling more scared than he does on screen, he says, "Andar se dara hua hoon! I believe for an star that fear and scare is very important when you go on the stage, and this is the role of Shri Ram, so all the more reason to get it right… In the subconscious mind it's always there that any mistake does not happen."

Notably, Drawing a parallel between stage and screen, he says, "You can't afford to go wrong or improvise and have to stay within the bound script and character. I can have all the experience, but after all we are humans and anyone can commit mistakes! I try to give my 100% and that has resulted in the success of my roles in Mirzapur The Movie , Maamla Legal Hai and Laapatta Ladies ."

As per the latest buzz, He recalls that being a son of a priest, he has grown up listening to tales of Shri Ram and Mahadev, and now he is getting the chance. "It's not only about that act – chahrey pe soumyata, shaleenta, saiyam, ekagrita, because you portray the character of puroshon mein uttam Shri Ram. The entire world will watch and on live telecast over 50 crore rupees people will watch it on Doordarshan, OTT and YouTube live streamings."

In further updates, On his prep, he says, "The great thing is that we are in Navratri and I am fasting, so with a shudh body and pure soul I will essay the role. title: Ektaa Kapoor announces The Dirty Picture 2, 15 years after Vidya Balan’s National Award-winning performance: ‘There is a story to tell’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Vidya Balan won her first National Movie Award for her iconic performance in Ektaa Kapoor's The Dirty Picture . Fifteen years after the movie's theatrical rollout, Ektaa has now revealed its sequel. However, she has not revealed any details about the movie, including its central character, cast or rollout date.

Adding to this, Vidya Balan won the National Award for Best Star for her performance in The Dirty Picture. Ektaa Kapoor announces The Dirty Picture 2 In conversation with Ranveer Allahbadia on his podcast, Ektaa shared that she had been considering a sequel for some time but decided to move ahead only after finding a story she wanted to tell audiences.

Meanwhile, "One very big movie I'm making is The Dirty Picture 2. I'm planning it after 15 years. This time, I believe there is a story I want to tell. The Dirty Picture was about Silk Smitha. It was about a woman who was condemned for standing up against her sexuality. Ab sexuality is about your choice. I never saw her as a victim. I saw her as someone who celebrated her sexuality, and the movie did so well," she shared.
Notably, Ektaa added that, like the original, The Dirty Picture 2 would also revolve around one person's story. However, she did not reveal whose life would be at the centre of the sequel.

As per the latest buzz, Vidya won the National Movie Award for Best Star for her performance in The Dirty Picture. In 2012, the star spoke about her experience of making the movie and the memories she cherished from the project.

In further updates, She shared, “I just knew one thing we all were trying to make a good movie as long as you know that nothing is in your control. I was saying to Milan (Luthria- director) that the movie has rolled out two months back and now I want to watch the movie again. We have such wonderful memories with this movie I would be glad to watch this movie on DVD.”

On top of that, "I think the biggest award was The Dirty Picture. I got an opportunity to play Silk and to work with this team is the biggest award. Everybody have loved this movie and we are grateful for that," she added.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday staged a protest and marched towards the Congress office, demanding action against Congress MP and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, who has been accused of sexual harassment.

Adding to this, The protest came after JNU terminated Akoijam’s services following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment involving female students. Meanwhile, “Rahul Gandhi has been shielding the professor accused of sexual harassment. Congress talks about ‘Ladki hoon, lad sakti hoon’, but it has not taken any action against the professor,” Leela Singh, a member of the BJP’s SC Morcha, told HT.
Notably, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj also criticised Gandhi for his alleged “double standards” and accused him of shielding a “predator” in the Lok Sabha.

As per the latest buzz, “An internal committee report found that all the complaints of sexual harassment lodged by female students against the sitting Congress MP from Inner Manipur, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, were true and recommended his dismissal,” Swaraj shared, according to news agency ANI.

In further updates, “I would like to ask if ‘smash the patriarchy’ is merely a political slogan. If not, why haven’t you taken action against your sitting MP yet? title: Nana Patekar’s autopsy CONFIRMS heart attack caused by blood clot in left main coronary artery: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nana Patekar was 75. He was declared dead at 5.10 am after doctors attempted to revive him through cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for around 45 minutes. The star was at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, when he as per reports fell unwell.

Adding to this, According to a PTI report, the postmortem examination found that Nana suffered an acute heart attack after a blood clot blocked the left main coronary artery. The artery supplies blood to a significant portion of the heart.

Meanwhile, The autopsy report recorded the cause of death as, “acute myocardial infarction due to left main coronary artery thrombosis secondary to atherosclerotic occlusive coronary artery disease, a natural cause of death”.

Notably, The findings establish that Nana's death was due to natural causes. Doctors had initially suspected a heart attack when the star was brought to hospital, but the postmortem examination later provided the specific medical cause.

As per the latest buzz, Nana as per reports became unwell at his home in Dona Paula. His caretaker contacted a private hospital and requested an ambulance. Since the star's residence was located less than a kilometre from the hospital, an ambulance was dispatched to the house.
In further updates, Medical personnel as per reports began resuscitation efforts after reaching the residence. Doctors continued CPR for approximately 45 minutes but were unable to revive him.
On top of that, Nana was subsequently declared dead at 5.10 am on October 8. His mortal remains were later taken to Goa Medical College and Hospital for the postmortem examination.
Following the star's death, his son Malhar Patekar travelled to Goa to bring his father's mortal remains back to Maharashtra.

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Monday backed his colleague Rahul Gandhi’s remarks that “this government will go”, in an apparent reference to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Centre amid intensified protests against the Election Commission over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Adding to this, Congress MPs Shashi Tharoor and Rahul Gandhi. In a post on X, the Lok Sabha MP from Thiruvananthapuram put up a post of Gandhi that shared in Hindi: “Gyanesh Kumar will go. This government will go. Then the repair of democracy will begin”.
Meanwhile, Separately, Tharoor also posted verses from a poem of Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar', "Janatantra Ka Janma" (जनतंत्र का जन्म / “The Birth of Democracy”)”.

Notably, “But earthquakes happen and tornadoes do occur, When people raise their eyebrows in rage, Give way, listen to the thunderous sounds of the chariot of time, Abdicate the throne, for the people are coming to claim it,” the poem read.

As per the latest buzz, Gandhi has been leading the ongoing INDIA bloc’s protests against Kumar and “vote chori” in recent days. On Monday, he asked the CEC to turn approver and resign as the Opposition's fight was against the bigger powers that were behind him.

On top of that, The Opposition has been demanding the resignation of the CEC after a report by The Indian Express shared Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times over the last 10 months, mostly to decisions and orders related to the SIR of electoral rolls.

title: Ranvir Shorey slams CJP's protest call, asks them to approach courts instead: ‘Hijacking the streets is the actual murder of democracy’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Ranvir Shorey has weighed in on the row surrounding the detention of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders ahead of their planned protest in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He argued that protesters should turn to the courts and democratic institutions rather than take to the streets. His remarks come amid criticism from several Bollywood actors, including Huma Qureshi , Sonakshi Sinha and Vijay Varma , over the authorities' handling of the demonstration.

Adding to this, Ranvir Shorey says protests should be the last resort in a democracy. Ranvir Shorey slams CJP for protesting On Sunday, Ranvir took to X and shared a video of CJP spokesperson Sourav Das appealing to citizens to take to the streets and not retreat. Reacting to the video, he wrote, "Show your numbers in Parliament and the ballot, not the streets! And if the way to those seems unjust, show the courts! That is the democratic way! Hijacking the streets and holding the public infrastructure and law and order machinery to ransom is the actual “murder of democracy”!"

Meanwhile, He added, "Protests in a democracy are meant to be a last resort. Not a way to circumvent the judiciary’s or legislative domain! Your “right to dissent” cannot turn into 7-days-a-week “protests” that hijack the country and make life hell for the rest of us! Only anarchists, attention seekers or morons would protest without exercising the legal remedies already available."

Notably, When an X user responded by saying that Ranvir did not know that the 'CJI has been compromised as well', the star appeared to mock the claim, writing, "Ever-growing list: I am compromised, Other voters are compromised, Media is compromised, Parliament is compromised, PMO is compromised, CEC is compromised, SC is compromised…Only daphli banging, dubiously funded mobs of parties that didn’t win elections on the streets are believable."

As per the latest buzz, The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, planned a protest in Delhi on October 10, 2026, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The demonstration was scheduled to take place at Jantar Mantar. However, ahead of the protest, Delhi Police detained Dipke and two other CJP leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, at Delhi airport shortly after they arrived from Mumbai. The three were later rolled out. Protests continued in Delhi on Sunday.

In further updates, On Monday, Ashutosh Ranka gave Delhi Police 24 hours to announce a date for a protest at Jantar Mantar, warning that the CJP would decide its next course of action if it did not receive a response within the deadline.

On top of that, Meanwhile, security has been tightened in central Delhi ahead of a protest march to the Supreme Court led by the INDIA bloc. Barricades have been erected at several locations, and entry and exit at certain metro stations will remain closed from 6 am to 4 pm on October 12, 2026, for security reasons.

title: 'Poora desh Jantar Mantar banega': Abhijeet Dipke as site loses ‘designated protest venue’ tag
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday reacted to the Delhi Police's decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue, saying the entire country would now become a site for demonstrations.

Adding to this, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke speaks to the media at Dr BR Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur, after being rolled out from the custody of Delhi Police. (ANI) “They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it’s no longer a protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!” Dipke wrote on X.

Meanwhile, The reaction came after a Delhi Police circular on Monday opened up that Jantar Mantar would no longer be a designated venue for protests and demonstrations. The circular also named three alternative locations for holding demonstrations in the national capital.

Notably, According to the Delhi Police circular, the Ministry of Home Affairs had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.

As per the latest buzz, Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a designated protest site. The three new venues identified for demonstrations are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in Shahdara.
In further updates, The circular shared detailed and revised standard operating procedures for organising protests at the three venues would be issued separately.

On top of that, Jantar Mantar has been a focal point of youth-led protests since June, led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Dipke. The demonstrations had previously drawn attention over alleged examination irregularities and demands for accountability from the government.

The site came into focus again last month after an investigative report raised questions about Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities. The report gave fresh momentum to Opposition allegations of “vote chori” (vote theft) linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

title: Gulshan Devaiah recalls weeping after Irrfan’s death, says he ‘didn’t know’ he liked the actor so much
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

From playing a menacing villain in Guns & Gulaabs to a caring partner in Badhaai Do, Gulshan Devaiah has shown his versatility as an star. Yet, across the many characters he has played, there is a certain stillness in his performances that brings to mind the late Irrfan . In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, Gulshan opened up about how the legendary star influenced his craft, admitting that while he has consciously and subconsciously picked up aspects of Irrfan’s acting, he has never tried to imitate him.

Adding to this, Gulshan Devaiah spoke about Irrfan’s influence on his acting. 'Irrfan has been a huge influence on me' When asked whether Irrfan had influenced his acting, Gulshan shared, “Absolutely, both consciously and subconsciously. I never try to copy him, but Irrfan was a huge influence on me throughout my career. Since I didn't go to drama school, I learned acting by observing great performers. However, I was very conscious that I didn't want to copy anyone — whether Irrfan, Manoj Bajpayee, Daniel Day-Lewis, Robert De Niro, or Kate Winslet. And that's how I learned.”

Meanwhile, Gulshan also spoke about the uniqueness of Irrfan’s performances and how, despite not fitting the conventional mould of a leading man, the star had an undeniable ability to draw audiences towards him.

Notably, He shared, “Irrfan had this quality that you didn't know what he would do next, and many times he didn't do much; he would hold back. Genetically, he had those big, god-gifted eyes that held your attention even when he was doing very little on screen. He used them really well. Sometimes he would deliver lines without even looking at his co-star. He was doing things that were really different. He would deliver dialogues differently, yet there was this magnetic attraction to him, and one wouldn’t say that he was not as good-looking as Hrithik Roshan or Shah Rukh Khan or Salman Khan, but somehow he would draw attention. So certainly, he was one of the greatest influences among many actors.”

As per the latest buzz, While Gulshan closely observed Irrfan’s performances to hone his own acting skills, he had not realised just how deeply connected he felt to the star until he heard of his death. Recalling his reaction to the news, Gulshan shared, “I remember weeping on the phone with my mother when the news broke. He was truly a one-of-a-kind star. This is why his death, not only for me, but for millions of people, felt very personal, like a family member has passed away. I was talking to my mother and weeping, and my mother was like ‘I didn’t know you liked him so much’, and I was like, ‘Yeah, neither did I.’”

In further updates, Gulshan is currently gearing up for the rollout of his next movie, Little Thomas, which follows a curious young boy who desperately wants a sibling. Directed by Kaushal Oza, the movie is set to rollout on October 23.

On top of that, Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. title: 'Cops slapped us, hit our private parts, took us 30-40 km away': Protesters detained in Delhi anti-EC stir
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The second day of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest witnessed detentions of more than 700 persons, some of whom were detained for almost seven hours, with their phones snatched and taken to detention centres, which are 30-40 km away.

Adding to this, Security personnel detain a demonstrator during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities linked to the "special intensive revision" (SIR), near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on October 11. (AFP) On Sunday evening, many lawyers and activists posted SOS messages on X and other social media platforms to seek help for the detainees.
Meanwhile, HT spoke to two of the detainees who shared how they were detained, targeted, assaulted and whisked off in prison vans to Pandwalan Khurd.

Notably, One of the detainees, Arjun Unnikrishnan (30), is a researcher and a lawyer who was at Connaught Place around 3-3.30 pm on Sunday to protest against the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, when he was detained. He shared he spent almost seven hours in detention in different parts, which was a complete nightmare for him.

As per the latest buzz, “I had just reached Connaught Place when my friends and I saw a group of police personnel detaining a couple. The police personnel then approached us and started pushing us. They shoved us inside a DTC bus along with locals who were not even part of the protest. We were taken close to Palika Bazaar side. Soon, the police started acting like mad people. They first made us sit on the road in rows. They snatched our phones...many of us had tried to record them. People who refused to share their phone passwords were humiliated and abused. Nobody had a choice,” Arjun told HT.

In further updates, “In front of me, a young boy was mentally tortured as they slapped him four times and then took his phone to open his phone's gallery. Almost 10 cops were looking at a young boy's phone and laughing. We were all very scared. Then, a senior officer came who pretended to be a good police officer as he scolded other officials and assured us we would be safe and rolled out if we cooperated. By then, we had been slapped and abused and were scared, so we agreed to cooperate,” he added.

On top of that, "But then, they brought in a jail van. We entered the jail van in a line. The moment we entered, we saw 3-4 police personnel. One by one, they slapped us, hit our private parts, and kicked us on the chest and back. Nobody could even run because it's a small, cage-like van. This was all in the middle of CP. There were four minors. I know this because when the police were taking our details, they revealed their names and ages. We raised our voice, but the police were not ready to listen," Arjun further shared .

He alleged that the detention bus took them from CP to Chhawla, where it halted for 10-20 minutes before leaving. By then, one of the protesters, who had managed to hide his phone, had contacted a lawyer and sent his live location.

I got a call from these guys and I got to speak to the director. We had a lot of chats, but before he had a conversation with me, he had watched most of my interviews and a lot of my movies. Notably, “Considering that there are no prohibitory orders under section 163 of the BNSS, we are of the opinion that the detention may not have been authorised… for the moment without entering into the row and the correctness of the detention order, considering that senior advocate appearing on behalf of the detainees gives an undertaking that the detainees would not protest at Azad Maidan, Panaji, tonight, we direct the PI Panaji Police Station to rollout the seven seven persons forthwith,” the bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar shared.
As per the latest buzz, The detainees were represented by senior advocate Norma Alvares.
In further updates, The protesters affiliated to the Cockroach Janta Party had planned a sit-in protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

On top of that, Among those detained was local CCP (Corporation of the City) corporator Jack Sukhija and Goa CJP unit lead protester Amreen Shaikh among others. Former Allahabad High Court chief justice Ferdino Rebello was among those who had gathered at the site in support of the movement.

title: 'Don't drag Supreme Court into politics': CJI Surya Kant amid Delhi protests row
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday shared the Supreme Court should not be “dragged into any politics” amid the ongoing protests against the alleged crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi, urging lawyers to ensure that the functioning of the top court and the movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants remains unhindered.

Adding to this, ‘SC can’t be allowed to become disruption site’: CJI after plea on Delhi police action (PTI) “There should not be any obstruction in the functioning of the court. There should not be any impediment in the movement of the lawyers, their clerks, court staff or litigants,” the CJI told Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai, who mentioned a fresh petition concerning the detention of lawyers and the suspension of internet services.
Meanwhile, Making it clear that the court had no objection to democratic activities, CJI Kant shared lawyers were free to protest but should do so at designated places.

Notably, “Every member of the Bar can also protest. Wherever there is a designated place to protest, you can protest,” he told senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, who also mentioned a separate petition for listing. CJI Kant added that he had already appealed to the protesters.

As per the latest buzz, The observations came a day after a special bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a series of directions to protect the right to peaceful protest, restore freedom of movement and ensure that no person was detained except in accordance with the procedure established by law. The bench also directed that metro and railway services operate normally, internet connectivity remain undisturbed and restrictions around court complexes be removed to ensure access to justice.

In further updates, Rai sought the listing of the SCBA’s fresh petition on Tuesday, when the court is scheduled to hear the other batch of matters arising from the protests. The CJI agreed to list the plea but asked the Bar to ensure that the court’s functioning was not affected.

On top of that, “Alright, we will list it. But you must also see that democratic activities take place smoothly. There is no difficulty with that. But just see to it that at least the Supreme Court functioning is not affected,” shared the CJI.
When Rai pointed out that the lawyers were protesting peacefully, the CJI reiterated his concern about the institution being drawn into the political contest surrounding the demonstrations.

title: Drishyam 3 worldwide box office collection day 10: Ajay Devgn film beats Border 2's lifetime haul in just 10 days
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window performance day 10: Ajay Devgn ’s Drishyam The Conclusion has emerged as one of the biggest box-office successes of 2026 so far. The crime thriller, billed as the final instalment in the Drishyam franchise, has crossed the ₹ 450 crore rupees mark worldwide within 10 days of its rollout. Despite a slowdown during the week, the movie has maintained a strong run and is closing in on the ₹ 500 crore rupees milestone. It has also secured the position of the second-highest-grossing movie of the year so far.

Adding to this, Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window earnings day 10: Ajay Devgn leads the thriller. Drishyam 3 worldwide ticket-window performance According to Sacnilk, Drishyam 3 collected ₹ 176.50 crore rupees net in India over its opening weekend, securing one of the biggest starts for a Hindi movie. It recorded the seventh-highest opening weekend for a Hindi rollout, coming close to the figures posted by Sultan while surpassing the opening-weekend collections of War and Tiger 3. The movie continued to draw audiences through the weekdays, with its collections witnessing only moderate declines. After wrapping up its first week with ₹ 245 crore rupees net in India, the Abhishek Pathak directorial began its second week on a strong note, earning ₹ 14.50 crore rupees on Friday.

Meanwhile, The thriller then added ₹ 49 crore rupees over its second weekend, taking its domestic net collection to ₹ 309 crore rupees. Its overseas performance has been relatively more restrained, although the movie has continued to register steady business in international markets. Trade sources indicate that it collected ₹ 6 crore rupees on its 10th day, pushing its overseas gross earnings to ₹ 109 crore rupees. With these figures, Drishyam The Conclusion has taken its worldwide gross collection to ₹ 479 crore rupees, bringing it within touching distance of the ₹ 500 crore rupees mark.

Notably, Ajay Devgn's Drishyam The Conclusion has not only become the highest-grosser of his career, but has also positioned itself as the second highest-grossing movie of 2026 so far. The movie surpassed the lifetime hauls of Sunny Deol, Varun Dhawan and Diljit Dosanjh's Border 2 ( ₹ 450 crore rupees worldwide) and Hanuman Ansh ( ₹ 435 crore rupees worldwide). It is now only behind Ranveer Singh and Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar The Revenge ( ₹ 1813 crore rupees worldwide).

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Abhishek Pathak, Drishyam 3 brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from the second part in a cameo.

In further updates, The story picks up six months after the events of Drishyam 2, with Vijay Salgaonkar (Ajay Devgn) and his family—wife Nandini (Shriya Saran), and daughters Anju and Anu—living under the shadow of the past murder case, waiting for the legal file to permanently close. Officer Rajveer reopens the cold case with fresh intent, targeting the local police station where Sam's body was hidden beneath the foundation years ago, hunting for fresh DNA or physical proof. The movie culminates in a high-stakes ego clash and courtroom/investigative showdown between Vijay and Rajveer, bringing a definitive stop to the franchise.

title: International organisations condemn detention of journalists during Delhi protests, urge police to uphold press freedom
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) on Sunday urged Delhi Police to refrain from targeting journalists covering protests in the capital and honour the government’s assurance to the Supreme Court that media personnel would not be impeded in performing their duties.

Adding to this, Security personnel detain demonstrators during a protest near Jantar Mantar on Sunday. (Vipin Kumar/HT) CPJ is a US-based independent organisation that documents attacks on journalists and advocates for press freedom worldwide. Other international organisations, such as Reporters Without Borders (RSF) and the United Nations Human Rights Office (OHCHR), also expressed concern.

Meanwhile, “At least six journalists, including those from mainstream news organisations such as The Indian Express and Hindustan Times, were temporarily detained by Delhi Police,” CPJ shared in a post on X.

Notably, “CPJ calls on Delhi Police to honour the government’s assurance to the Supreme Court that journalists will not be impeded in their professional duties and to refrain from targeting journalists covering the protests,” it added.

As per the latest buzz, They shared India, as the world’s largest democracy, had a special responsibility to uphold press freedom and protect journalists’ constitutional right to report without interference.

In further updates, These detentions took place during the October 10 protests, planned by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

On top of that, Authorities imposed curbs without precedent in Delhi, ordering the gates of 45 metro stations to be shut, cutting mobile internet across central Delhi, cancelling trains into the city, deploying more than 40,000 Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) personnel, and installing barricades and spike strips ahead of the protest.

There were reports of journalists being detained around Jantar Mantar. Posts and videos on social media showed the detained journalists flashing their press cards from the buses transporting detainees.

title: Shekhar Suman defends public's right to protest peacefully amid anti-CEC protests: ‘I see it as a very positive thing’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The past few days have seen several Bollywood celebrities voice their support for protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Shekhar Suman , who often incorporates political satire and commentary into his show Shekhar Tonite , of late spoke about the public's right to dissent peacefully.

Adding to this, Shekhar Suman hosts talk show called Shekhar Tonite. 'Protests are right if carried out peacefully' During his recent appearance on The Lallantop, Shekhar shared in Hindi, which translates to, "Protests are a part of politics, and they are also a part of society. We have been protesting ever since we were growing up. When we don't get something, we start protesting at home, saying that we want this or that. If protests are carried out peacefully and do not turn violent, I think they are absolutely right and should take place. When you don't get something the way you want it, you have to put in a little more effort and raise your voice for it."

Meanwhile, Citing Mahatma Gandhi, Shekhar shared the freedom fighter taught people to fight for what is right. He added, “If your demands are not being met, you should start protesting. When the people raise a collective voice, the government also pays attention to it. And this should continue to happen. Every person should be able to protest for what they believe in, wherever they are and whatever their position in society may be. I see it as a very positive thing in society."

Notably, Of late, Bollywood star Sanjay Dutt appeared on Shekhar Suman's show. However, the star found himself at the centre of a row after saying that he no longer felt peace in India. He had shared, “The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I can’t feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people, and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shivji that those days come back soon.”

As per the latest buzz, Sanjay's remarks sparked row, with several social media users criticising him. The star, who as per reports holds a 10-year UAE Golden Visa, later issued a clarification, saying his words had been misinterpreted. He also described the conversation on the show as 'scripted'. Meanwhile, Shekhar defended the star, saying that Sanjay has 'huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen.'

title: Lawyers' group tracks detainees, ensures paperwork, issue SOPs amid Delhi protest crackdown
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A distress call came around 11pm on Sunday. Thirty to 40 people were being held at Najafgarh in southwest Delhi, five or six of them minors, and some claiming to be injured. Within minutes, a message went out to lawyer groups. By the time Shobhit Chaudhary had spoken to the police point of contact, independent lawyers near Najafgarh had been located and dispatched.

Adding to this, Police detaining a protester during the protest in New Delhi. (AP) “We basically worked on creating a rapid response system for the fraternity,” shared Chaudhary, a Delhi-based independent litigator. “It is working, but in all honesty there should not be a need for this to be working.” Track all updates from protests against Gyanesh Kumar here

Meanwhile, He is part of a legal volunteer network that has worked around the clock over the last few days to help protesters amid mass detentions in the Capital over protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Notably, On Sunday, the Supreme Court held a special sitting and ordered that peaceful, unarmed protesters not be detained except through the procedure established by law, and that normal metro and rail services and internet connectivity be restored. The detentions continued regardless.

As per the latest buzz, As the Delhi Police detained thousands on Saturday, many were stopped at checkpoints while trying to enter central Delhi. The detainees included leaders of student organisations and political parties.

In further updates, Chaudhary shared he began efforts to help the detainees, starting alone during the July protests when people hit the streets to demand the resignation of the then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan . Other independent lawyers reached out, and a group was formed. It now has “somewhere above 70 to 80” lawyers, spread across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Assam and Delhi National Capital Region.

On top of that, Each lawyer brings their own network of friends, batch mates and colleagues, which allows a distress call to be pushed quickly to whoever is nearest the site. “It is more like a message delivery mechanism, where we can find out which lawyers are near the area,” Chaudhary shared.

The group circulates phone numbers on WhatsApp and Instagram, along with two short messages. One tells people what to do if they are detained. The other tells them what to do if they see someone else being detained: Movie the bus and note the number plate.

title: Delhi court discharges UK national of flag insult charge; frames UAPA charges over alleged presence at 2023 London protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A Delhi court discharged Inderpal Singh Gaba, a UK national accused of involvement in twin violent attacks at Indian High Commission in London in March 2023, of the offence of insulting the Indian national flag, noting the alleged offence was committed by a foreign national on foreign soil.

Adding to this, The NIA case relates to protests outside the Indian High Commission in London on March 19 and 22, 2023. (AP File photo) The court, however, ordered framing of charges against Gaba under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), holding his alleged participation in a protest where pro-Khalistan slogans were raised, and his standing on the Indian flag fell within the definition of “unlawful activity” under the anti-terror law.

Meanwhile, The case pertains to the National Investigation Agency (NIA) probe into two incidents outside Indian High Commission in London on March 19 and 22, 2023 by a group of protestors, who pulled down the Indian flag and attempted to hoist a Khalistani flag, besides assaulting security personnel.

Notably, NIA claimed the violent protests were connected and led by Britain-based Sikh radical Avtar Singh Khanda (now dead) in retaliation to Punjab police ’s action against Waris Punjab De chief Amritpal Singh and his associates. Gaba had allegedly taken part in the March 22 protest. Gaba was arrested at Attari border on April 25, 2024 and was charged by NIA under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 and section 13 (1) of the UAPA (promoting unlawful activities).

As per the latest buzz, Advocate Arun Khatri, who appeared for Gaba, argued that “there was no material to connect him to the two incidents.” “The alleged desecration of the flag had taken place in London and that the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 did not extend beyond India’s territory,” he argued.

In further updates, In an order on October 8, reviewed by HT, a special NIA court at Rouse Avenue Courts held that the 1971 law has no extra-territorial jurisdiction and cannot be invoked against Gaba for an alleged act committed in London, even though it shared it was satisfied through video recordings that he committed the offence. “Although this court is satisfied from video recordings of the incident dated March 22, 2023 that Gaba, by standing on the Indian National Flag, which was lying on the ground, has committed an offence under section 2 of the Prevention of Insults to National Honours Act, 1971 but still he cannot be tried for the shared offence before this court,” the court ruled.
On top of that, However, it found sufficient grounds to charge him under section 13 (1) of UAPA.
Khatri told HT: “We will challenge this order in the high court.”

title: Delhi protest LIVE: INDIA bloc's SC march underway; Rahul Gandhi to file petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi protest LIVE: Opposition parties led by Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi are marching to the Supreme Court to raise the issue of “vote chori”. Gandhi shared earlier that he would file a petition at 3pm in the top court against “vote chori”. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders, including Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, visited the Parliament Street Police Station today to seek a date for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The CJP has also given the Delhi Police 24 hours to provide a date to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. ...Read More

Adding to this, Opposition's march to Supreme Court Opposition parties marched to the Supreme Court today. Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge had earlier sought a meeting with CJI Surya Kant to raise allegations of "vote chori". However, the CJI declined to meet Rahul Gandhi over the allegations. People familiar with the matter shared the decision was based on the pending cases before the Supreme Court and the CJI's role in hearing petitions concerning the issue. The Opposition had planned to raise several concerns, including police action against protesters demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, the need for an early hearing of cases linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the composition of the committee responsible for recommending appointments to the Election Commission. Capital crackdown On Saturday, authorities carried out an unprecedented security operation and detained more than 7,000 protesters, including CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke and four former chief ministers. The action prevented a planned mass demonstration at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of CEC Kumar. Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site, remained largely deserted throughout the day. More than 30,000 security personnel were deployed, while multiple layers of barricades were set up across Lutyens' Delhi to prevent protesters from reaching the area. On Sunday, more than 200 protesters were detained as they shouted slogans and marched towards Jantar Mantar, with several seen being taken away in police buses. The action came as the CJP's protest entered its second day. The detentions continued into the evening, with protesters being picked up from different locations even after 6.30 pm. Why Gyanesh Kumar is under fire The protests against Kumar come amid growing criticism of the Election Commission over the SIR of electoral rolls. The row gained momentum following reports that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months to decisions and orders, some of which they as per reports shared were issued without their knowledge. The Election Commission, however, has maintained that the three-member poll panel took all decisions, including those related to the SIR, unanimously.

Meanwhile, Delhi anti-CEC protest LIVE: A group of lawyers have started gathering outside the Supreme Court. This includes Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s legal team. The lawyers are waiting for Gandhi to arrive along with senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi.
Notably, Delhi anti-CEC protest LIVE: As huge crowd gathers for INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court, lawyers are also joining in.

As per the latest buzz, Delhi anti-CEC protest LIVE: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has joined the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court. “The agitation and sit-in protests will continue. It is our responsibility to save democracy; the BJP, in collusion with the Election Commission, seeks to destroy the Constitution and democracy. They want to remain in power forever. They create fake voter lists, cast bogus votes, and fabricate election result,” Yadav shared.

In further updates, Delhi anti-CEC protest LIVE: A large crowd gathers at the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction in New Delhi as opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, prepare to march to the Supreme Court. The leaders are finalising their strategy at the Constitution Club, while security personnel remain deployed at the site.

On top of that, Delhi anti-CEC protest LIVE: INDIA bloc leaders are on their way to the Supreme Court where they will file a petition against ‘vote chori’. Visuals showed the bus moving through massive crowd and police deployment ahead of the petition filing.

Delhi anti-CEC protest LIVE: All matters pertaining to alleged discrepancies in the voters’ list and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) are before the top court and should be pursued through judicial proceedings, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant told Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi as he declined a request for a meeting amid nationwide protests.

title: Supreme Court stresses due process as detentions continue; Opposition and CJP vow to press on with protests in Delhi
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A phalanx of 40,000 security personnel detained roughly 700 people on Sunday as sporadic protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar continued to bubble up across the Capital for a second consecutive day as the Supreme Court underlined that detentions must be lawful and traffic movement eased with the metro running and fewer road barriers.

Adding to this, Security personnel detain demonstrators during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities linked to the "special intensive revision" (SIR), near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi (AFP) The leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) –– a satirical movement that forced the education minister’s resignation three months ago –– were rolled out after signing a bond promising “to maintain peace and good behaviour” for one year. But a day after their dramatic detention from a flight, the CJP leaders shared they’ll press on with the protests and seek permission on Monday for a new stir.

Meanwhile, “The CJP will neither back down nor be intimidated…we will hit the streets again,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared on X before heading back to Maharashtra to deal with a bereavement. Dipke also shared he had not signed a bond barring him and other CJP leaders from staging further protests.

Notably, Monday will also see the Opposition return to the streets with a march to the Supreme Court. Leaders of the INDIA bloc shared they had an appointment to meet Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday afternoon but court officials denied the claim.

As per the latest buzz, The developments came a day after security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress to thwart the planned protest, launching an unprecedented clampdown that saw the detention of 7,000 people, internet services suspended near Jantar Mantar, cancellation of many long-distance trains to Delhi and the controversial closure of 45 Metro stations.

In further updates, In addition, right-wing groups thrashed many protesters in front of the police, laid spike strips on arterial roads, erected thousands of yellow barricades that choked traffic, and put up loudspeakers that blared prerecorded police warnings against unlawful gatherings.

On top of that, Sunday was relatively calmer, with the Metro open, trains back on track and some roads opened. But central Delhi was shrouded in a security blanket even as some protesters made it past barricades for short-lived agitations that melted away as police bundled them away into buses, triggering allegations of brutality. Many journalists and bystanders were also picked up, sparking a row.

Sanjay Kumar, who was visiting Delhi from Bihar, shared, “I had come for an excursion to the India Gate on Sunday but police shared I would not be able to sit on the lawns, or even walk to monument. They asked us to take a photo and leave.”

title: Vidyut Jammwal says Bollywood can't compete with Hollywood using money: 'Just by spending money, you cannot create phenomenal stuff' | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Vidyut Jammwal has been working in Indian films for 15 years, starting out as a villain and later carving a niche for himself as an action star. The star is now making his Hollywood debut with the newest adaptation of Street Fighter. The 45-year-old plays Dhalsim in the multi-starrer movie. Ahead of its rollout, the star speaks to Hindustan Times about the differences between Bollywood and Hollywood, and what he hopes to achieve now.

Adding to this, Vidyut Jammwal is set to make his Hollywood debut with Street Fighter. Bollywood can't compete with Hollywood using just money Having worked in Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu films for 15 years, Vidyut admits the Hollywood experience was very different from what he is used to. He says, “It’s very different from what we have here. Yes, the money they spend is phenomenal, but just by spending money, you cannot create phenomenal stuff. You see a different kind of planning, professionalism, discipline, and legal aspects. They are very particular about what they do. That is a big difference.”

Meanwhile, In the recent past, many Indian filmmakers have mounted films on massive budgets, believing that the extra expenditure would allow them to give their films the quality needed to bridge the gap with Hollywood. However, Vidyut disagrees with this notion. He says, “If a person suddenly gets a lot of money, it doesn’t mean they will suddenly learn manners, too.” The star clarifies that the statement is not a dig at Indian cinema. “I am not talking just about our industry, but about people in general, too. Money is not everything. There is a certain mindset change that needs to be brought,” he adds.

Notably, Vidyut says that the standards of action in Indian films have improved in the last few years. “Things have changed. We are doing excellent,” he says, adding, “The standard of action is very high here now. We get the best action directors in our films now. I get the opportunity to work with everybody who is big in India, also.” But the action star says that Hollywood differs in their approach to filming it. “The only difference there is the legal system. The laws are very strict, the insurance companies are very fastidious about what the star can do,” he says.

As per the latest buzz, Street Fighter is the third live-action feature-length movie based on the Street Fighter video game series by Capcom. It features a large ensemble cast, including Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Roman Reigns, David Dastmalchian, Cody Rhodes, Eric André, Andrew Schulz, Vidyut Jammwal, 50 Cent, and Jason Momoa. Directed by Kitao Sakurai, the movie will rollout in theatres on October 16.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. title: Ektaa Kapoor admits 2008 was the worst year of her professional career: ‘I didn’t respect the professionals who came in at that time’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ektaa Kapoor has established herself as a name to be reckoned with in Indian entertainment. In a journey that has spanned from TV to films and eventually OTT, she has been everywhere. The year 2025 marks three decades since Ektaa entered the entertainment industry. In a new chat with Ranveer Allahbadia, Ektaa shared that the form was not always great as in 2008 she had the worst year in her professional career.

Adding to this, Ektaa Kapoor of late opened up that Lock Upp will be back with season 2. What Ektaa shared During the interaction, when Ranveer asked what happened in 2008, Ektaa shared, “2008 was the worst year for me career-wise. That one year was very strong because nothing was going right for me. That year was really bad for me professionally. Mental health wise it was bad because I was not able to grapple with that. But the COVID time affected me the most mentally. Even though I didn’t give birth to my son, I had postpartum of my own. I was grappling with motherhood. I had never been stuck at home for so long, and I had never seen so much death around me. 2021-2022 was mentally the toughest year for me, and 2008 was the toughest professionally.”

Meanwhile, She went on to detail where she went wrong and how she found a lot of good mentors along the way who helped her. “I had fewer things on paper back in 2008. Never work without having things on paper. Secondly, when you work with companies and you trust in professionals, professionals might leave the job, and then the company will change a professional, and you will be stuck. You have to be a little more cognizant of the fact that you have to build relationships beyond success. I used to believe I was the shiz. I am not the shiz. I can do great work, and I can do bad work. People should want to work with me beyond the good and bad… Overconfidence is not swag; it’s stupidity. You don’t need overconfidence to build momentum. I learnt humility, teamwork, and putting things on paper from that patch. I had some really big mentors on the way. I met Uday Shankar; he taught me so much about work ethic. I met a great number of strong professionals and learned that respect is mutual. Form can always be up and down, but your credibility cannot; your level of ethics cannot. People should not wait for your downfall,” she added.

Notably, Some of the iconic Television shows that Ektaa has created include Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii, Kasautii Zindagii Kay, and Pavitra Rishta. She of late produced the reality television series Lock Upp through her production house, Balaji Telefilms. Season 2 was revealed a few days ago.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Union Minister Chirag Paswan on Sunday claimed that CJP's protests in Delhi over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise were an attempt to "create anarchy" in the country, and hailed the central government for bringing the situation under control.

Adding to this, Chirag Paswan also criticized the Congress for allegedly causing trouble for Delhiites by staging demonstrations (Hindustan Times/Santosh Kumar) He also criticized the Congress for allegedly causing trouble for Delhiites by staging demonstrations on the same issue for the last several days and charged the grand old party with "remaining silent on allegations of sexual assault by a JNU professor who happens to be its MP".

Meanwhile, The comments come days after the chief of LJP (Ram Vilas), an ally of the ruling NDA, had shared cancelling trains cannot stop India's youth in an apparent reference to the security clampdown in the national capital in view of the October 10 CJP protest .
Notably, He had also lambasted the opposition parties for allegedly spreading false narratives and playing politics with demonstrations against the Election Commission.

As per the latest buzz, "We consider protests to be legitimate when people put forward their views peacefully. But if anti-social elements use agitation as a pretext to pursue their own agenda, it becomes necessary to identify them. I believe that yesterday's protest was meant to promote anarchy.
