Adding to this, Tanushree Dutta offered prayers to Mahakal after Nana Patekar's death. What Tanushree shared In the video, Tanushree was seen offering prayers in front of the Mahakal idol. In the caption, she began, "Mahakal Baba ke darbar mein meri astha ! He is the one who saved me from the multiple attacks on my life and shielded me from hundreds of maaran kriyas done by Nana and his friends.

Meanwhile, What a coincidence that I got to visit Mahakal right after such a positive development in my life. Even though I seriously have my doubts on the authenticity of the death news. I really wish and hope truly this evil is dead and gone for good and that all the evils of my life die off one by one."

Notably, She went on to add, "If you love me you will make all the Evils dead that have decided to afflict me and who will not stop unless they are dead. All of them including their flying monkeys and helpers and supporters jinke shay mein these evils have continued to afflict me.

As per the latest buzz, I cannot fulfill my purpose in the world and I will leave from here if these people still continue to breathe. I want all of them gone and with full confirmation of their demise. I cannot take their extreme negativity and persistent conspiracies anymore."

In further updates, She added, “My ride is coming and unless this wish is fulfilled I'm not staying on Earth. Its either them or me here on Earth Baba. Infact in space, I can connect better with you. Earth is overrated and I have no real incentive to continue to live here. Har Har mahadev! Mahadev, I want you to prove to the world that you love me and how much! For Aeons I have been your devotee. I'm demanding this now from you with that birthright. They don't recognise me but you do, so please accept my humble request.”

On top of that, Nana Patekar died on Thursday morning at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. His son, Malhar Patekar, verified that the star died on October 8. He was found unconscious at his residence and was subsequently rushed to Manipal Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.

Tanushree accused Nana of sexual harassment on the set of the 2009 movie Horn 'Ok' Pleassss. In 2018, during the Me Too movement, the claim became public. An FIR was registered against Nana, who denied the allegations. In 2019, the case was closed for lack of sufficient evidence. title: Nana Patekar death: Autopsy report confirms actor died of heart attack caused by blood clot in coronary artery
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star Nana Patekar died on Thursday morning at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa. As per the latest update from news agency PTI, the autopsy report on the mortal remains of star Nana Patekar has verified that he died of a heart attack, a senior doctor at the state-run Goa Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) shared on Sunday.

Adding to this, Nana Patekar was last seen in the movie Subedaar. (AP Photo/) What the doctor shared According to the doctor, the veteran star suffered a heart attack caused by a blood clot blocking the left main coronary artery, which supplies blood to a large part of the heart. The postmortem report cites the cause of death as "acute myocardial infarction due to left main coronary artery thrombosis secondary to atherosclerotic occlusive coronary artery disease, a natural cause of death".

Meanwhile, Doctors at the hospital shared the star's caretaker had approached the medical facility and requested an ambulance, saying Nana Patekar was unwell. An ambulance was sent to his apartment, located within a kilometre of the private hospital.
Notably, Despite being administered cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for 45 minutes, Patekar could not be revived and was declared dead at 5.10 am, a doctor had shared, suspecting a heart attack.
As per the latest buzz, His mortal remains were subsequently taken to GMCH for an autopsy.

In further updates, Nana Patekar's son, Malhar, had arrived in Goa to take his father's body back. The body was taken to Pune before being transported to his farmhouse in Donje village, where he was cremated with full state honours.

On top of that, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar, Union Ministers Ramdas Athawale and Murlidhar Mohol, Lok Sabha MP Sunil Tatkare, NAAM Foundation co-founder and star Makarand Anaspure, FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, star Jackie Shroff, and several personalities from Bollywood, politics, sports and other fields attended his funeral.

Nana Patekar had a career spanning more than four decades across Hindi and Marathi cinema. He also worked as a writer and director and was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2013 for his contribution to cinema and the arts.

title: Bleeding protesters, detained journalists: New Delhi sees fresh chaos despite SC order
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Fresh chaos gripped New Delhi district on Sunday as several groups protested against the Election Commission and police continued their crackdown, apprehending people, including journalists, despite a Supreme Court order against illegal detentions.

Adding to this, Police officers detain a demonstrator from National Students' Union of India (NSUI), outside the Press Club of India, in New Delhi on Sunday. (Reuters) The journalists – including one from a national daily, from digital news platforms and camera persons – were detained from outside the Press Club of India on Raisina Road, Connaught Place and RK Ashram Marg. More than 70 people were held outside the Press Club of India.

Meanwhile, A bus packed with the detainees at Connaught Place included two journalists and at least two protesters who were bruised and bleeding. Overall, about a 100 protesters were packed into two buses and removed from the area. A man was pulled out of a burger joint on suspicion of being a protester. A video of the incident showed him telling the cops that he was simply standing at the spot and that he would not go with the team. The cops later let him go.

Notably, The police action came despite the top court’s order earlier in the day that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained except in accordance with the “procedure established by law”. The court also shared the police cannot detain such peaceful protesters beyond the area covered by a prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
As per the latest buzz, Besides, AISA president Neha Bora and CPI(M) leader John Brittas were detained at Connaught Place. Brittas suffered injuries after he was dragged by the security personnel.

In further updates, The protesters are seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls.

On top of that, On Saturday, about 41,000 security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress to thwart a planned protest, launching an unprecedented clampdown that saw the detention of 7,000 people and left large chunks of Delhi deserted.

Four former chief ministers and the leaders of the CJP were among those detained as police cracked down on students, lawyers and politicians, successfully refusing passage to Jantar Mantar. Yet, sporadic protests bubbled up at different points of the city throughout the day, even as police rushed to smother the stirs.

title: Gulshan Devaiah says people should rally behind Ramayana 'whether you like it or not', compares Ranbir Kapoor film to SS Rajamouli's RRR | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Gulshan Devaiah was lauded for his portrayal of the evil King Kulashekara in Rishab Shetty's mythological action drama Kantara Chapter 1 . In an exclusive conversation with Hindustan Times, the star of late discussed the challenges of portraying mythological characters on screen. He also spoke about Ranbir Kapoor's highly anticipated Ramayana and expressed support for its global ambitions, saying Indian films that aim to reach audiences worldwide deserve encouragement.

Adding to this, Gulshan Devaiah spoke about Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana. 'There is nostalgia attached to Ramayana' When asked if actors face difficulty convincing audiences while playing mythological or fantastical characters, Gulshan shared, "I don't think so. Kantara was a work of fiction; with regard to the Ramayana, there is already a lot of literature. I don’t think it’s difficult. Also, people come to theatres with the mindset that it’s make-believe, but still, if you make them feel the story and the scene, they will give you the benefit of the doubt."

Meanwhile, Gulshan shared that several factors contribute to a mythological movie's convincing quality. He shared, "It also depends on how good a movie is shot, the performances and other things in order to keep that illusion going. I don’t think playing mythological characters or historical characters is that difficult unless there are some expectations. For example, certain characters are very revered and divine, like Shivaji Maharaj; he is almost a divine person for Maharashtrians, so to interpret him becomes tricky."

Notably, The star pointed out that audience expectations and emotional connections to familiar portrayals can make certain roles more challenging. Speaking about Ranbir Kapoor's portrayal of Lord Rama in Ramayana, he shared, "Even Rama has that (baggage of expectation) because (he is called) maryada purushottam . There is nostalgia attached to it also because there is an entire generation that has very fond feelings for Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan and Arun Govil playing Lord Ram, so you tend to measure that old feeling with this."

As per the latest buzz, Gulshan also discussed the global ambitions of Ranbir's Ramayana and how they set the movie apart. He shared, "I think this movie caters to a much larger audience, to the Indian diaspora and to the non-Indian diaspora audience as well. The ambition is to go global. Also, people can say a thousand things about it, but I think that having an ambition like this is not a bad thing. Like there is no bigger market than Hollywood for English films, so if an Indian movie has that ambition that everyone in the world should watch it, then it’s a great ambition."

In further updates, Gulshan also urged audiences to support Indian films that aim to reach viewers worldwide, regardless of their personal opinions. Citing SS Rajamouli's RRR as an example, the star shared the movie's success in the US was a positive development for Indian cinema.

On top of that, He shared, "Whether you like it or not, that's a different thing, but one should rally behind it. Like, I didn't really vibe with RRR, but I love that it did so well in the US. It is good for Indian films that at least Rajamouli has his foot in the door, and more will follow. Ramayana seems to be that, so for an ambition of our movie to go global and still rooted in our culture, it is good."

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The adaptation of the Hindu epic is planned as a two-part cinematic project, with the first instalment scheduled for a Diwali 2026 rollout.

title: Ujjwal Nikam reveals conditions he put before makers of Rajkummar Rao's Prahaar: ‘Use real names, no glorification’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Rajkummar Rao's next movie, the much-awaited Prahaar - The Ujjwal Nikam Story, is based on the life of Ujjwal Nikam, who represented the prosecution in the trial of Ajmal Kasab, the lone surviving terrorist of the 26/11 Mumbai attacks. During a recent interaction, Nikam revealed the condition he had set before agreeing to let the makers adapt one of the most significant chapters of his career and life for the big screen.

Adding to this, Rajkummar Rao plays lead role in Prahaar. 'There should be no glorification' In conversation with India Today, Nikam shared, "My first condition was that there should be no glorification of any character, including myself. I also told them to use real names of all the characters who had participated in this legal proceeding and the makers took no objection certificate from the concerned people, including the judge, Mr Madan Laxmandas Tahaliyani."

Meanwhile, Praising Rajkummar Rao for his dedication to portraying him on screen, Nikam shared, "Let me praise Rajkumaar Rao. He lived like Ujjwal Nigam. He would emphatically forcefully say points of the submission, he brought in that same josh otherwise Rajkummar is a very silent and soft person. So, I was shocked when I saw the trailer and other things, the other lawyers asked me whether Raj was moving along with me, I shared no."

Notably, During the same conversation, Rajkummar opened up that he had not met Nikam before filming because the lawyer was busy. Instead, the star watched videos of Nikam's courtroom arguments to prepare for the role.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Avinash Arun and produced by Dinesh Vijan under Maddock Films, Prahaar – The Ujjwal Nikam Story is a biographical courtroom drama starring Rajkummar Rao as public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam. The movie focuses on Nikam's role in the prosecution of Ajmal Kasab in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks case. It also stars Wamiqa Gabbi, Jaideep Ahlawat, Sikandar Kher and Ashish Vidyarthi in pivotal roles. The movie is scheduled to rollout in theatres on October 16, 2026.

In further updates, Rajkummar was last seen in the Netflix movie Toaster, co-starring Sanya Malhotra. Apart from Prahaar – The Ujjwal Nikam Story, he has several projects in the pipeline, including Raftaar, the biopic of former cricketer Sourav Ganguly titled Dada: The Sourav Ganguly Story. He also has the third movie of his hit franchise Stree.

On top of that, Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows. A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today. At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through movie reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, star interviews, and trend-driven stories. title: Vidyut Jammwal says time, not talent, separates Indian and Hollywood action films
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, Star Vidyut Jammwal believes Indian cinema has the ability to create action spectacles just like Hollywood as both industries work with the same pool of technicians with the key difference being the time and resources available to execute their vision.

Adding to this, Vidyut Jammwal says time, not talent, separates Indian and Hollywood action films Jammwal, who is making his Hollywood debut with "Street Fighter", the live-action adaptation of the popular video game of the same name, gave the example of SS Rajamouli's "Baahubali" franchise.

Meanwhile, "We work with the same technicians as they do, and there is no difference. In my movies, I've worked with the best in the world and they are the same people who work over there. I think the difference is that what we shoot in 10 days, they shoot in four months. The liberty of time, the luxury of spending too much time to create something is what they have that we don't normally use.

Notably, "But now that's what we are doing. If you see movies like 'Baahubali', they have taken a while to be made. And because they have taken a while, you can see the results," the star, best known for headlining action movies such as "Force","Commando" franchise, and "Khuda Hafiz", told PTI in an interview.

As per the latest buzz, In "Street Fighter", Jammwal features alongside a star-studded Hollywood cast of Andrew Koji, Noah Centineo, Jason Momoa, Callina Liang, Roman Reigns, Orville Peck, Cody Rhodes, Andrew Schulz, Curtis "50 Cent" Jackson and David Dastmalchian.

In further updates, The movie, directed by Kitao Sakurai of "Bad Trip" and "Aardvark" fame, is set in 1993 and follows estranged fighters Ryu and Ken , who are recruited by Chun-Li to compete in the World Warrior Tournament.
On top of that, However, the competition takes a dangerous turn as they uncover a deadly conspiracy that forces them to confront each other and their pasts.

The 45-year-old star shared he had never planned to work in the West and viewed it as another step in his career, much like his foray into the South Indian movie industry, where he featured in Telugu and Tamil films such as "Sakthi", "Thuppakki" and "Madharaasi".

title: Karnataka CM Shivakumar, Congress MLAs to travel to Delhi to protest against electoral roll SIR
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar on Sunday shared he and all Congress MLAs would travel to Delhi to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that one crore rupees voters had been removed from the state’s electoral lists without verification.

Adding to this, Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar will join Congress MLAs in Delhi on Monday to oppose SIR, alleging mass voter deletions and raising concerns over democratic rights. In conversation with reporters in Mysuru, Shivakumar shared he had instructed all Congress MLAs to be in Delhi to defend voters’ rights. The party would organise its own campaign rather than join the protest organised by other groups, he shared, adding that the Congress did not intend to mobilise a large crowd.

Meanwhile, “Tomorrow (Monday), we will fight in our own way. I have instructed all our MLAs to be in Delhi. We do not want a large number of people to go. Our MLAs will be in Delhi. I am also going to Delhi. We will fight for the rights of voters. Our hope is that the rights of every voter in the country should be protected and they should get the right to vote. We cannot delete the names of voters from the list,” he shared.

Notably, Shivakumar shared the question of whether the organisers had secured permission for the Delhi protest was separate from the manner in which the authorities had responded to it. He shared the restrictions imposed at the outset, the internet shutdown and the detention of people as they arrived by plane raised concerns about democratic freedoms. The arrest of elected representatives in such circumstances, he added, was embarrassing for the country.
As per the latest buzz, “The Prime Minister should answer whether there is democracy or an emergency in the country. Let us give him time,” he shared.

In further updates, India was recognised internationally as a leading democracy, Shivakumar shared, warning that incidents involving restrictions on protests could damage that reputation. He shared those in power should be prepared to face public criticism instead of preventing people from expressing their views.

On top of that, “In a democracy, protesters have the right to protest. They have their own voice. No one can suppress that voice. Let them protest. If you are in power, answer all their questions. Give them a chance to meet the Election Commission. Let them meet the leaders,” he shared.

Shivakumar shared people in public life had to accept criticism and acknowledge their mistakes when they had done something wrong. The treatment of protesters, he shared, reflected an atmosphere of fear in the country.

title: Normal metro, free movement, undisturbed internet: Supreme Court's 5 directives on Delhi curbs amid protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Supreme Court on Sunday held a special hearing on the curbs across Delhi amid calls for protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and shared that metro and train services shall be restored to normal and no illegal detentions should take place in the capital.

Adding to this, On Saturday, about 41,000 security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress. (REUTERS) The top court ordered that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained except in accordance with the “procedure established by law”.

Meanwhile, Supreme Court 's directions come after a special bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard on Sunday petitions alleging mass detentions, restrictions on movement, suspension of internet services and non-compliance with the court’s October 9 order on transport curbs ahead of Saturday’s protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Notably, "Senior counsels submitted there was a flagrant violation of the directions -- metro railway was not functioning, New Delhi and Nizamuddin railway stations remained closed, no traffic advisories were issued and a large number of persons were subjected to undue harassment and illegal detention even beyond the area which was covered by the prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023," the bench shared during the urgent hearing.
As per the latest buzz, (i) Metro and rail facilities shall function normally until and unless regulations required to be imposed keeping in mind disturbance to public order as under Article 19(2).

In further updates, (ii) Free movement of people in the city shall be permitted subject to traffic regulations. Imposition of barricades shall be reviewed forthwith keeping in mind law and order and other traffic conditions.
On top of that, (iii). Internet facilities shall remain undisturbed
(iv) Smooth movement of people in the city shall be permitted in accordance with law.

title: Delhi police register 20 FIRs over Jantar Mantar protest attempts
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi police registered more than 20 first information reports (FIRs) over attempts to hold a protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Saturday despite restrictions imposed by the force, senior officers shared.

Adding to this, Security personnel stand guard near Janpath Metro Station. (PTI) “More than 20 FIRs have also been registered in connection with alleged attacks on police personnel during the demonstrations, with police citing attempts to disrupt law and order and obstruct government officials from performing their duties,” an officer shared.
Meanwhile, The action comes amid heightened security in the Capital, particularly around Jantar Mantar, where police had not permitted the proposed protest.
Notably, Police cited security concerns, the sensitive nature of the area, and the presence of important constitutional institutions and government offices while justifying the restrictions.
As per the latest buzz, Police also warned on Friday that any attempt to assemble in violation of the restrictions, obstruct public movement or engage in violence would invite legal action.

In further updates, Security personnel were deployed at key roads and intersections, while barricades, police vehicles and additional forces were positioned to prevent protesters from reaching the designated area.

On top of that, Police shared the restrictions were necessary to prevent a repeat of the violence during an earlier Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest in July opposing National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) irregularities, when more than 200 police personnel were injured, according to the police.

The proposed protest on Saturday was called by CJP and supporting student organisations to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

title: No illegal detention of protesters in Delhi; metro, internet to run normally: Supreme Court
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Supreme Court on Sunday ordered that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained except in accordance with the “procedure established by law”, while further directing that metro and railway services in Delhi operate normally, internet connectivity remain undisturbed and free movement of people be restored.

Adding to this, Policewomen try to prevent a detained protestor from escaping in New Delhi on Saturday. (Reuters) The court also ordered authorities to remove a notice imposing prohibitory restrictions around the Supreme Court and other court complexes to ensure unhindered “access to justice”.

Meanwhile, A special bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the directions after an urgent hearing on petitions alleging mass detentions, restrictions on movement, suspension of internet services and non-compliance with the court’s October 9 order on transport curbs ahead of Saturday’s protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Notably, The bench directed that metro and rail facilities run normally unless restrictions are required to address a public order situation within the framework of Article 19(2) of the Constitution. It further ordered that people’s free movement in the city be permitted subject to law, internet services remain undisturbed in accordance with law, and no person be detained except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly in the case of peaceful, unarmed assemblies beyond the area covered by a prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

As per the latest buzz, It went on to issue notices to the alleged contemnors in the contempt proceedings, including the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), the concerned railway authorities and Delhi Police, seeking their responses to the allegations of non-compliance with its October 9 order.

In further updates, It directed the authorities to file short affidavits in response to the contempt pleas and submit compliance reports detailing the steps taken to implement Friday’s directions on regulated metro and rail services and the publication of traffic advisories.

On top of that, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta disputed the allegations, maintaining that metro services had operated normally on Saturday, although entry and exit had been restricted at 45 of the network’s 303 stations. The bench sought details of the affected stations and directed the authorities to file their responses by Tuesday, while listing the matter for October 13.

The court also directed the authorities to take down the notice or any such imposition of Section 163 BNSS in and around the Supreme Court complex, saying the measure was necessary to remove any apprehension regarding access to the Supreme Court or any other court of law.

title: Salman Khan claims some actresses pay paparazzi to take photos of them from behind: ‘Do it if you want to’

Notably, Salman also urged photographers to respect celebrities’ choices about how they want to be photographed. He pointed out that some celebrities invite photographers and pay them to take certain kinds of pictures, while others are uncomfortable with such images.

As per the latest buzz, He shared, “Some women and some guys call them there, pay for them to be there, and ask them to do this. So what can the paps also do then? The differentiation is between those who want and those who don’t want it. Those who are okay with it can continue, but those not okay, should not be troubled. So when you girls come there and ask them not to click a photo a certain way, after that, if they do so, then I shall deal with them.”

title: India rejects UN rights body’s remarks on Delhi protest detentions as ‘unwarranted interference’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

India on Sunday described the UN human rights’ agency’s remarks expressing concern at the detention of thousands of protesters in New Delhi as unwarranted and an unacceptable interference in internal affairs, and accused the body of “extreme selectivity” in its response to events in the region.

Adding to this, The external affairs ministry accused the UN human rights body of double standards after it raised concerns over mass detentions during Saturday’s Delhi protests. (PTI) Police detained more than 2,000 protesters as security forces locked down central parts of the national capital on Saturday to thwart a rally demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner over alleged irregularities in voters’ rolls.

Meanwhile, The remarks by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) about the events in New Delhi are “unwarranted and constitute an unacceptable interference in the internal affairs of India”, the external affairs ministry shared in a note.

Notably, The ministry argued that India is the largest democracy with the right to peaceful assembly guaranteed by the Constitution and “safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media”. It shared that, as in every democracy, Indian citizens “exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order and safety”.
As per the latest buzz, “Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances,” the statement shared.

In further updates, The ministry accused OHCHR of having “an approach of extreme selectivity” in its public positions, and noted that violent responses to protests in India’s neighbourhood had “gone uncommented, as indeed have law enforcement actions in its own vicinity”.
On top of that, “Such double standards only erode the credibility of its standing and contribute to the loss of faith in multilateralism,” the statement shared.

In a statement issued in Geneva on Saturday, OHCHR expressed concern at “reports of mass detentions in India of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists” during large-scale demonstrations in New Delhi.

title: NAPA seeks probe into 'police action' on Sikh devotees at Bangla Sahib during Delhi protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chandigarh, The North American Punjabi Association on Sunday expressed concern over reports of police action on Sikh devotees at the historic Gurdwara Bangla Sahib in New Delhi during Saturday's protest and demanded an independent, time-bound inquiry into the incident.

Adding to this, NAPA seeks probe into 'police action' on Sikh devotees at Bangla Sahib during Delhi protest It also sought clarification regarding a video purportedly showing Delhi Police personnel entering the Bangla Sahib wearing shoes while going to detain protesters who had taken shelter there.

Meanwhile, NA Executive Director Satnam Singh Chahal shared allegations of disrespect towards Sikh religious traditions, forcible removal of turbans and rough handling of women protesters had caused concern among Sikhs in India and abroad.
Notably, He shared the turban was an important symbol of Sikh identity, dignity and faith, and any allegation of its forcible removal during police action should be investigated seriously.
As per the latest buzz, Chahal also called for an inquiry into allegations that women protesters were mishandled and that police personnel ignored their requests for help.
In further updates, Acknowledging the police's responsibility to maintain law and order, NA shared the incident should be examined through a fair and impartial investigation.

On top of that, The association also referred to the Delhi Police's clarification that footage showing personnel wearing shoes was recorded in a common passage leading to the designated shoe-removal area.
It called for an examination of complete, unedited footage and all relevant evidence to establish the facts.

title: Hanuman Ansh actor lauds Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for reciting Hanuman Chalisa after attack: ‘Made our faith unshakeable’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar has become a hero to people around the world after saving the lives of 174 passengers despite being stabbed mid-flight. During a conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi from his hospital bed, Smit spoke about how reciting the Hanuman Chalisa gave him strength during the life-threatening ordeal. Now, Hanuman Ansh star Shobhinaw Satyaa has lauded the pilot for sharing his faith with the world, saying it has made believers' faith even stronger.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh star Shobhinaw Satyaa lauds Captain Smit Machchhar. ‘He made our faith unshakeable’ In conversation with India Today, Shobhinaw shared, “We have grown up listening to stories of bravery. But those stories often made us feel that such things happened a long time ago, that there were people like that in the past. Incidents like these remind us that heroes still exist.”

Meanwhile, Shobhinaw emphasised that Smit’s account of how his faith helped him face a life-or-death situation had strengthened the belief of many. He shared, “The bigger thing was that he also made us realise the power of the Hanuman Chalisa. When that man recited the Hanuman Chalisa there, he touched upon something that is a matter of faith for us. I thanked him a lot for bringing this out in the open. He made our faith, which was already so strong, even more unshakeable.”

Notably, During a video call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Smit spoke about his experience and what gave him the courage to act during the incident. “I was fighting for my life. I realised at that time that if I won't show courage, then 170 passengers will lose their lives,” Machchhar told the Prime Minister.
As per the latest buzz, Smit’s Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked him in the cockpit during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, leaving him seriously injured. The aircraft then went into a steep descent.

In further updates, In conversation with the Prime Minister, Smit recalled realising that the aircraft was going down and gathering his strength to open the cockpit door despite his injuries. “I knew that the aircraft was going down ... I had fallen to the ground. I told myself that the door is right there, just open it. I managed to do it, and people entered,” he shared.
On top of that, Passengers then entered the cockpit and helped restrain the suspect. The aircraft was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely.

title: Delhi markets to reopen on Sunday amid protests, traders urge vigilance and security
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Several markets in Delhi have decided to reopen on Sunday, urging traders to step up security and remain vigilant amid a tense situation following Saturday’s crackdown and heavy security deployment across the Capital. The decision comes as the CJP and student groups have called for another round of protests at Jantar Mantar on Sunday, raising concerns over potential disruptions during the festive shopping season.

Adding to this, Connaught Place, Khan Market and Sarojini Nagar traders are pushing to resume business amid protests, urging vigilance and police support to ensure normalcy. Atul Bhargava, who heads the New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA), shared that a fresh advisory had been issued to markets. “This is the festival season and a lot of stock purchases by traders have already been made. We have asked the markets to re-open today but they must increase the vigilance. Deploy people near entrances to check no rowdy element is creating ruckus. A lot of chaos was seen in Connaught Place on Saturday but we can’t keep asking people to shut their shops,” he added.

Meanwhile, “Looking at the ongoing protests & sensitive situation in and around Connaught Place on Saturday. We request everyone to be vigilant & cautious while re-opening on 11/10/26. Please keep your doors on guard and let us be alert and safe,” the advisory to the New Delhi markets reads.

Notably, “Yesterday, we kept the market on wait and watch mode. Shops were opened after closure of three hours. Police was able to contain the protest. We have decided to remain open on Sunday,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, Ashok Kalra, general secretary of the Sarojini Nagar market, echoed the same sentiments, citing fears of business losses. “Navratri have started and this is the peak sale season for us. Our market is fully open and we urge customers to come. Yesterday, we witnessed sharp drop in footfalls. We are also urging police and authorities to help ensure normalcy,” he added.

In further updates, Brijesh Goyal, who heads the Chamber of Trade and Industries, shared that retail markets would remain partially open due to uncertainty in the wake of the protests. “There was hardly any business yesterday. Not just retail trade, but including service sector, hospitality sector, transport, tourism, business has been affected across. Closure of markets during the festival has given a huge shock to traders.”

title: Jantar Mantar stays barricaded, 30 traffic choke points flagged as Delhi braces for more protests today
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Security arrangements remained in place across the Capital on Sunday, for a second consecutive day amid possibility of fresh protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with the Delhi Traffic Police warning of likely disruptions at 30 key points from 6am.

Adding to this, Police shared that 7,000 people were detained in Delhi amid CJP's Jantar Mantar protest on Saturday. The restrictions, which will be enforced depending on the prevailing situation, are likely to affect several stretches in New Delhi and Central Delhi, including roads around Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street and key government establishments. Commuters have been advised to avoid non-essential travel and keep additional time in hand, particularly if travelling to railway stations, inter-state bus terminals (ISBTs) and the airport through these areas.

Meanwhile, The 30 locations flagged by the traffic police include the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Patel Chowk, Windsor Palace, Rail Bhawan, Gol Dak Khana, Mandi House, Jhandewalan and Panchkuian roundabouts, besides the Tolstoy Road-Janpath crossing and the Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing.

Notably, Other stretches where traffic may be regulated include Dhaula Kuan flyover, Lodhi Road flyover, the approaches beneath the Bhikaji Cama Place and Moti Bagh flyovers, and the Ring Road-San Martin Marg T-point. Traffic movement may also be affected at the Minto Road-Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg junction and the Outer Circle of Connaught Place at its intersections with Barakhamba Road, Sansad Marg and Chemsford Road.

As per the latest buzz, On Sunday too, Jantar Mantar and its approach roads remained barricaded, while security personnel remained deployed at key intersections across central Delhi. The New Delhi district remains divided into 20 zones, each headed by a deputy commissioner of police-rank officer, with barricades installed at 37 identified points to prevent protesters from entering the area.

In further updates, On Saturday, about 41,000 security personnel turned the Capital into a fortress to thwart a planned protest demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged regularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The forces launched an unprecedented clampdown that saw the detention of 7,000 people and left large chunks of Delhi deserted.

On top of that, Four former chief ministers and the leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) – a satirical movement that forced the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan three months ago – were among those detained as police cracked down on students, lawyers and politicians, successfully refusing passage to Jantar Mantar. Yet, sporadic protests bubbled up at different points of the city throughout the day, even as police rushed to smother the stirs.

Reeling, the CJP revealed a second consecutive day of stirs on Sunday, when the Supreme Court will also hold a special sitting to hear pleas filed against the controversial crackdown. The Opposition – which had brought central Delhi to a halt last week – has already declared fresh protests from Monday.

title: Dhruv Rathee released late on Saturday, hours after being detained ahead of CJP protest: Officials
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Germany-based YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was rolled out late on Saturday, 18 hours after he was detained and prevented from participating in the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)’s protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. (PTI) According to officials, Rathee was rolled out at 3am and handed over to his family. He was apprehended from his residence in Kendriya Vihar society in Gurugram sector 56 at around 9.30am on Saturday.
Meanwhile, Rathee kept under the watch of the crime branch officials at one of their offices in Gurugram, the officials shared.

Notably, “Yes, he has been set free. His family members had arrived at a crime branch office where he was kept detained. Afterwards, he was handed over to them,” a senior officer of Gurugram police shared.

As per the latest buzz, “The step was taken after discussion with Delhi police and we were assured that he won’t be part of a group or mob trying to create law and order problem in the national capital amid the situation when prohibitory orders were already in force there,” the officer added.

In further updates, Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Suraksha Sanhita, a person can be temporarily detained for a maximum of 24 hours before producing them before a magistrate – unless it is under special laws.

On top of that, "He can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders," an unnamed police officer was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.

On Saturday, police stepped up security across the national capital to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar for a demonstration demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

title: Indians deserve answers: Probe alleged foreign links to Gen Z protests, identify backers
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

New Delhi : India cannot afford complacency about attempts by external actors to manipulate its political debate, weaken confidence in institutions or exploit domestic grievances. Covert foreign sponsorship of political mobilisation would compromise that accountability by allowing undisclosed interests to influence public decisions without accepting responsibility for the consequences. Therefore, protecting the electoral mandate from external disturbances requires an effective capacity in the law enforcement agencies and counter intelligence agencies to identify and investigate organised interference.

Adding to this, Connaught place barricaded ahead of the CJP protest (HT File) Concerns about such emerging foreign interference are visible in Indian political commentary and social media. They centre on the interaction between overseas commentators, international advocacy networks, digital platforms and domestic protest movements. Several reports establish that these concerns exist, and many people openly share them. Their seriousness should be assessed using the available evidence and proper legal investigations before it is too late.

Meanwhile, There are reports indicating that the ongoing so-called Gen Z movement is an externally supported attempt to destabilize India. Social media statements claim that it was described as a “cross-border influence operation” targeting India and the elected Modi government. These statements reflect growing tension in India about foreign involvement entering mainstream political debate.

Notably, The transition of the ongoing movement from online satire to street mobilisation gives the row practical significance. The Associated Press reported its first major physical protest in June 2026 and quoted its social media call to turn the joke into a revolution. Digital communities can evidently become organised political pressure through planned external support, as has been seen in different countries where elected governments have been overthrown through violent street protests. That raises questions about financing, account administration, promotional spending, and organisational direction, particularly when a newly propped-up social group with political objectives acquires substantial reach before establishing transparent structures. Therefore, it is critical to examine all these aspects before lending political legitimacy to the leadership of such a movement.

As per the latest buzz, Overseas commentators on India’s internal political and security issues also play an important role in this debate. Publications and interviews by Left-Communist-Islamist western media advance a strongly critical interpretation of the ruling government in New Delhi and its policies. Some reports have alleged that overseas funding and commentary, including work associated with such media, contributed to electoral interference in India. Another example is YouTube vloggers within India and abroad who have been creating propaganda videos to provoke the Indian audience. Videos like why the "Modi Govt is scared of Cockroach Party" shows how influential vloggers can amplify an anti-government movement and frame its political significance in India. This kind of communication can connect domestic controversies with overseas audiences, including the Indian diaspora. Key questions include undisclosed sponsorship, coordinated distribution of social media content, and operational links.

In further updates, Furthermore, Pieter Friedrich, referred to in some reporting as Peter Friedrich, was named in Delhi Police’s allegations about the 2021 farmers’ protest toolkit. He has been openly running hate propaganda not just against the Indian government but against the Indian diaspora, especially members of the Hindu community, in the United States. His name appears in almost all major anti-India protests in the US, and his open support for banned secessionist outfits in India is already known. The activities of these individuals raise a genuine question about why foreign citizens are so aggressively involved in spreading dangerous propaganda against a democratically elected government in India. More importantly, who is supporting their activities, and what is the end goal? The so-called ‘Gen Z revolutions’ in countries like Nepal and Bangladesh have only caused political and economic disruptions without any good governance benefits. Several reports indicate likely involvement by western foreign entities and oligarchs in both countries, leading to street violence and overnight uprooting of elected political representatives. Similar scenes are currently played out in France and Belgium where Communist-Islamists are riding on the student protests to weaken the incumbent regimes through breakdown of law and order and chaos.

On top of that, Foreign actors seeking political leverage could exploit dissatisfaction through concealed funding, fabricated material, coordinated accounts, or inflammatory messaging. Repetition across videos, articles, and social platforms could make a coordinated campaign appear as spontaneous public consensus. Overseas audiences can help circulate messages, support advocacy and attract international attention to domestic disputes in India. If those channels are covertly directed or financed, they could enable external interests to influence Indian politics through intermediaries.

Manipulated mobilisation could intensify social divisions, encourage confrontation and impede government processes in India. When demonstrably false claims or deliberate incitement by vested interests accompany mass protests, risks could extend to street violence and political instability. However, addressing genuine grievances also reduces opportunities for external actors to exploit them.

title: Imran Khan exclaims 'Jai Hind' as cops prevent him from leaving after detention, says he was driven around in police van for 2 hours. Watch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Imran Khan was among the 400 people detained by the Mumbai Police on Saturday in connection with participation in an anti-CEC protest at August Kranti Maidan. The star was later rolled out along with his girlfriend, Lekha Washington , and cousin Zayn Marie Khan. However, videos shared by protesters detained along with him show that police tried to stop him from leaving.

Adding to this, Imran Khan was detained briefly in Mumbai after participating in the anti-CEC protest on Saturday. Imran Khan confronts cops A series of videos shared by a protester named Lalit Sharma, who was also detained in Mumbai on Saturday, show Imran having various exchanges with the police officers. In the first video, Imran walks off into a dimly lit lane, with cops surrounding him. At one point, the police personnel try to form a human chain to stop him. Lekha and Zayn are seen in the video recording all this and asking the policemen to provide them with a warrant or proper documents. The next video shows the police personnel walking back as Imran waves to them and loudly exclaims, “Jai Hind!”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lalit Sharma (@adv_lalit_sharma_)

Notably, Lalit, whose Instagram profile lists him as a lawyer in the Bombay High Court, later spoke to Imran in a third video where the star detailed his experience after being detained. “I honestly don't know why I have been brought here. They picked us all off the streets. They shared gaadi mein baitho (sit in the van). I thought it must be a very nice car from the inside, that's why they are excited,” the star shared. Imran added that he and his companions were driven around in the police van for about two hours before being rolled out at an undisclosed location.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lalit Sharma (@adv_lalit_sharma_)

In further updates, Hundreds of people were detained at August Kranti Maidan, the proposed protest venue, and Nana Chowk in the vicinity. August Kranti Maidan holds historical significance as the site from which the Quit India Movement was launched in 1942. The gathering had been called by Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, in support of the CJP's demand for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid a row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Tushar Gandhi was detained while heading towards the site and was later rolled out by the Mumbai Police. The police informed that over 400 people were detained in the city during the demonstration.

On top of that, Mumbai Police have since registered an FIR at Gamdevi Police Station under Sections 223 (disobedience to an order), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 189(3) and 189(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Mumbai Police shared on Saturday. Police personnel themselves were the complainants.

title: Farmers stopped at Noida-Delhi border amid CJP protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

title: After CJP, Opposition calls for protest, march to Supreme Court to demand action against SIR
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Adding to this, Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi being detained during a sit-in protest against Chief Election Commissioner. (X/@INCIndia) INDIA bloc leaders shared they will urge the apex court to expedite cases related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the Election Commission (EC).

Meanwhile, Congress general secretary K C Venugopal shared, “We appeal to every Indian concerned about the survival of Indian democracy to join us in a massive protest march in Delhi on Monday - against the nationwide Vote Chori orchestrated by the Modi-Shah regime.”

Notably, Venugopal, one of the key strategists behind the Opposition’s protest plans, added, “INDIA MPs, leaders, workers and all concerned citizens will be holding a huge protest march against Gyanesh & Co, and a delegation of our senior leaders will submit a memorandum to the Hon’ble CJI for his intervention in this crisis.”
As per the latest buzz, “In the history of the country, no political delegation has ever marched to the Supreme Court. It will be unprecedented,” shared another senior leader, requesting anonymity.

On top of that, Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal shared the country’s youth had awakened and demanded Kumar’s resignation. Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee shared protests would continue in Delhi.

Kharge, who chaired the INDIA bloc meeting that finalised the protest plan, shared the government was detaining people questioning its actions. “Our youth, students, lawyers, journalists, social activists, farm union leaders, YouTubers, content creators, everyone who is questioning this regime are being detained. The Modi Govt has turned the ‘Mother of Democracy’ into a ‘Muzzled Democracy’! The cowardice of the BJP-RSS is on full display today,” he posted on X.

title: Gulshan Devaiah says violence dominating Bollywood is an ‘illusion’: ‘Amitabh Bachchan, Amol Palekar coexisted’ | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Gulshan Devaiah has played some of the most memorable villains on screen, from the destructive Kulasekhara in Rishab Shetty’s Kantara : Chapter 1 to the brutal Four-Cut Atmaram in Raj and DK’s web series Guns & Gulaabs. Lately, however, the star has also been exploring family entertainers and lighter stories. In an exclusive conversation with Hindustan Times, Gulshan says the shift was a conscious adjustment rather than part of a master plan. He wants his filmography to reflect his own tastes as a moviegoer, allowing him to explore different genres rather than be defined by a single role.

Adding to this, Gulshan Devaiah spoke about his new movie Little Thomas. (Instagram/ Gulshan Devaiah) His soon-to-release movie, Little Thomas , is a movie about a curious boy who desperately wants a younger brother. At a time when big-screen conversations are often dominated by violent, high-octane entertainers, the movie offers a different kind of story for families to watch together. Gulshan, however, believes that films across genres have always coexisted and that the industry's apparent shift towards hyper-masculine violence may not tell the whole story. Excerpt:

Meanwhile, Several, actually. I really enjoyed Taare Zameen Par — the concept was wonderful. My father was a big fan of animated films, so one of my earliest cinema experiences was watching Disney's Lady and the Tramp around 1984 or 1985. I really enjoyed watching those films; they transported me to a happy, imaginary world. Even now, my wife and I love watching animated films together, especially cat stories.
Notably, In Indian cinema, Taare Zameen Par stands out. I also remember Mani Ratnam's Anjali. That movie had a huge impact on me — it was about an adorable child who dies and makes us all sad.

As per the latest buzz, I think so. When we say a 'kids movie', it is usually a family movie, because 10- or 12-year-olds won't go to the cinema on their own. But I think all kinds of films have always coexisted. Currently, there is a lot of diversity in what audiences get to watch. It is just that these mass entertainers, which draw large crowds, are popular for obvious reasons. They are fun. Violence can also be fun. Great directors have used it as a medium, and it can be a lot of fun, but the business aspect of these films gets highlighted so much -- they make enormous amounts of money -- that it creates an illusion that the entire industry is shifting in one direction. But that's just an illusion.

In further updates, Like in the 1970s and 1980s, Amitabh Bachchan's "angry young man" was popular with the masses, while Amol Palekar's "average young man" thrived with the middle class — both coexisted and thrived. India has immense socioeconomic diversity, so different types of films that appeal to different audiences can coexist. A movie doesn't need to make ₹ 500 or ₹ 1000 crores to be a success; the return on investment ratio matters.

On top of that, One shouldn't pay too much attention to these things because nobody really knows what works. Like, until Hanuman Ansh started making so much money, I didn't even know it was in cinemas. Also, if a movie like 12th Fail can become the most successful movie of Vidhu Vinod Chopra's career of 35 years, so anything can happen. Hyper-masculine violence is a trend today, just as it was in the 70s and 80s, but other stories continue to thrive alongside it.

I used Hanuman Ansh merely as an example of a project that came out of the blue and achieved massive box-office success. We have seen similar films before, like Queen. Nobody thought that it would be such an enormous success, or Vicky Donor, for that matter. These examples have always existed; I spoke about Hanuman Ansh as a recent example.

title: CJP protest LIVE: ‘Haven’t signed any bond’, says Abhijeet Dipke, vows to ‘hit the streets again’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Security personnel detain student activist Neha Bora during the demonstration in New Delhi on Sunday. CJP protest LIVE: Delhi Police continued its clampdown across central Delhi on Sunday, keeping Jantar Mantar sealed, maintaining barricades at the capital’s borders and diverting traffic at 30 points, as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) vowed to resume its protest for the second straight day after an estimated 7,000 people were detained across the city. ...Read More

Adding to this, Student activist Neha Bora was detained after marching towards Connaught Place and then running towards H Block. She was detained inside H Block around 3 pm. CJP's presser Addressing the media on Sunday, Cockroach Janta Party co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka claimed that an “emergency-like” situation had been created in the national capital. They questioned the Delhi Police’s treatment of peaceful protesters and the government’s deployment of excessive force, as well as the shutting down of train services and metro stations. Das also shared he suspected that their phones had been hacked or cloned and that evidence had been planted. He added that the protests will continue until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns and urged the youth to continue protesting peacefully on the streets. What's happening at Jantar Mantar Delhi Police on Sunday continued to detain protesters, including CPI(M) leader John Brittas, around Connaught Place as groups returned to renew their demonstrations against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, even as the Supreme Court ordered that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained except through the “procedure established by law”. About 100 protesters were packed into two buses and removed from the area. At least four journalists were also detained briefly at RK Ashram before being rolled out. Several empty buses for transporting detained people were also spotted, as the crowd increased in the area. The fresh round of restrictions comes as CJP leaders insist they will not back down until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. While security restrictions will continue, the curbs on metro and rail services are being lifted. CJP vows to return to Jantar Mantar Ajinkya Shinde, who was designated by the group to lead the agitation after its leader Abhijeet Dipke was taken into custody, shared protesters would attempt to reach Jantar Mantar again on Sunday and continue their agitation until their demands were met. “The government thought we would back down after the detention of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. But we won’t. We will continue our agitation till Gyanesh Kumar resigns,” Shinde shared. AISA president Neha Bora also revealed the protest would continue in a late-night post on X on Saturday. “Let a hundred Jantar Mantars bloom! Another part of Delhi will become Jantar Mantar tomorrow,” she shared. 40,000 security personnel deployed across Delhi Police will try to prevent protesters from gathering at Jantar Mantar or entering the New Delhi district on Sunday. Movement on key roads will be regulated depending on the situation on the ground, officials shared, adding that police and Central Armed Police Forces personnel would remain deployed until the situation eased. More than 40,000 security personnel were deployed on Saturday, including 26,000 reinforcements. It was the largest such deployment in Delhi since February 2020. Jantar Mantar, the intended site of Saturday’s demonstration, remained sealed, with even journalists barred from entering. Loudspeakers at three entry and exit points broadcast warnings in Hindi and English. Restrictions on gatherings, processions and road blockades under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita will remain in force until further orders, officials shared. At the borders with Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, police have set up two tiers of barricades at Chilla, Ghazipur, Apsara and Singhu. Local police and paramilitary personnel will continue to man these crossings on Sunday. Metro and train services return to normal The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) shared in a post around 10 pm on Saturday that the entry and exit gates of all metro stations had reopened. Neither the DMRC nor the Delhi government's excise department had received a request from Delhi Police to close metro stations or liquor shops on Sunday as of Saturday. Northern Railway's chief public relations officer shared the restrictions on rail services applied only until Saturday. Traffic restrictions, however, will continue. The Delhi Traffic Police will divert vehicles from 6 am on Sunday at the same 30 points as on Saturday, “depending upon prevailing situation”. Opposition protest on Monday Meanwhile, the INDIA bloc has revealed a separate protest for Monday, with top opposition leaders set to march to the Supreme Court and urge it to expedite cases related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and the Election Commission. Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee was detained on Saturday during a silent protest outside the residence of Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee on South Avenue. She was taken to Dwarka in a prison van. Banerjee shared Rahul Gandhi had asked her to stay in Delhi for Monday's march.
Meanwhile, CJP protest LIVE: Opposition leaders to march to Supreme Court tomorrow, will meet CJI after 4 pm.

Notably, “Delhi Police fortified Central Delhi to stop people from reaching Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site. Result - There are now 50 different Jantar Mantars in and around Central Delhi,” he wrote in a post on X.
As per the latest buzz, “Congratulations @DelhiPolice for screwing up once again :)”
In further updates, He shared visuals from Surajmal detention center.
On top of that, CJP protest LIVE: RJD MP Manoj Jha visited CPI (M) MP John Brittas at RML hospital.
John Brittas was admitted to RML hospital for an X-ray scan to examine any injuries to his chest.

title: India hits back at UN rights office over remarks on Delhi protests, calls concerns ‘misplaced’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

India has rejected the UN Human Rights Office’s (OHCHR) remarks on the events in New Delhi, calling its concerns “misplaced” and accusing it of unwarranted interference in the country’s internal affairs.

Adding to this, Security personnel keep a vigil at Jantar Mantar road after a protest call by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll irregularities, in New Delhi. (PTI) In a statement shared by the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in Geneva on X, India shared the right to peaceful assembly was guaranteed by the Constitution and safeguarded by the country’s institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media.

Meanwhile, “We have seen the OHCHR’s remarks about today’s events in New Delhi,” the mission shared, adding that citizens exercise their right to peaceful assembly subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order.
Notably, “The authorities, for their part, act in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for redressal of any grievances,” it shared.

As per the latest buzz, India also called on the OHCHR to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere, arguing that the UN body should act in keeping with its mandate of impartiality and non-selectivity.

In further updates, The response came after the United Nations expressed concern over mass detentions in Delhi amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstrations have been accompanied by heightened security measures and restrictions in parts of the national capital.

On top of that, The protests, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other groups, are linked to demands for Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Delhi Police denied permission for the CJP’s proposed October 10 demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing short notice, alleged violations during earlier protests and concerns over public safety, traffic and law and order.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

title: Drishyam 3 box office collection day 9: Ajay Devgn film shows growth on 2nd Saturday, crosses ₹285 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Drishyam 3 ticket-window earnings day 9: Ajay Devgn in a still from the movie. Drishyam 3 shows growth For Ajay Devgn, Drishyam 3 registered the biggest opening of his career. The advance bookings for Drishyam The Conclusion opened on September 27, and the movie went on to collect ₹ 27 crore rupees before its rollout. By the end of the day, the movie went on to collect ₹ 66.75 crore rupees net across India. This is the third biggest opening by a Hindi movie ever and the biggest in Ajay Devgn’s career. On Saturday, the movie collected ₹ 53.50 crore rupees, and showed huge growth on Sunday, bringing in ₹ 61 crore rupees. Monday saw a dip with ₹ 21 crore rupees but the movie remained steady all week and ended its first week haul at a staggering ₹ 245.50 crore rupees.

Adding to this, The latest update from Sacnilk states that Drishyam 3 has collected ₹ 26.50 crore rupees on its 9th day of rollout, which is its second Saturday. Since it is a weekend, the collections were expected to grow and with Dussehra still a week away, Drishyam 3 is set to utilise the free weekend at the ticket-window to its full potential. This brings the total India net collection to ₹ 286.50 crore rupees so far.

Meanwhile, With this, Drishyam 3 has now surpassed the record set by Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior. The 2020 historical drama is no longer Ajay's highest-grossing movie, with a lifetime collection of ₹ 279.59 crore rupees in net collection. Drishyam 3 is Ajay's highest-grossing rollout now.

Notably, Drishyam 3 brings back Ajay Devgn’s Vijay Salgaonkar, along with Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, and Kamlesh Sawant. Saurabh Shukla also reprises his role from the second part in a cameo.

title: Delhi protests: UN 'concerned' over mass detentions, seeks immediate release of detainees
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The United Nations on Saturday expressed concerns over "mass detentions" in Delhi amid the ongoing anti-CEC protest. The international organisation called on the authorities to uphold the people's right to assemble peacefully.

Adding to this, Protesters being dispersed by Delhi Police amid CJP Protest at Connaught Place, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI) The remarks came as Delhi Police detained over 4,000 people marching towards Jantar Mantar to hold a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the function of the poll body.

Meanwhile, In a press rollout issued amid ongoing detentions in Delhi, the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, shared, “We are concerned by reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during today’s large-scale demonstrations in Delhi.”

Notably, UN human rights spokesperson Thameen Al-Kheetan also urged the authorities to "exercise utmost restraint" in tackling the protesters. "We also urge the authorities to engage in meaningful dialogue to address the broadly held concerns expressed," it shared.

As per the latest buzz, The CJP had planned to stage a demonstration at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi. However, Delhi Police denied permission for the protest, while heavy security and roadblocks prevented most demonstrators from reaching the site.
In further updates, The group shared its founder, Abhijeet Dipke, and two other leaders, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained shortly after their flight from Mumbai landed in Delhi.
On top of that, Delhi Police have not issued a public statement on their detentions.

title: Tanushree Dutta compares Nana Patekar with Raavan, hits back at criticism over her remarks on his death: ‘Not scared to speak truth’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Nana Patekar died in the early hours of October 8 in Goa at the age of 75 from a cardiac arrest. Tanushree Dutta , who had accused the star years ago of sexual harassment on a movie set, made an ‘evil dead’ remark after his death. She received flak for it, and has now made another video to hit back at the criticism for her comments.

Adding to this, Earlier, AICWA lashed out at Tanushree Dutta over ‘Evil Dead’ remark on Nana Patekar’s death. What Tanushree shared Tanushree shared a live video where she doubled down on her remarks on Nana Patekar. She shared that if people are so concerned about her speaking ill about someone after their death then they should stop burning effigies of Raavan too. She then callled him ‘shaitaani, cunning, manipulative, shaatir dimag, jhootha (wicked, liar).’

Meanwhile, The star shared, "Yeh apne haathon mara hai, agar mara hai toh. I am little bit doubtful. Kyunki jaise Sushant Singh Rajput-Disha Salian ka case nikal aaya hai, toh bahot saare log expose hue hai aur bahot hie gehri investigation chal rahi hai. Toh dur dur se bhi kisika connection hai toh uska aaj nahi toh kal naam aane wala hai. Toh mujhe thoda doubt hai yeh sachme mara hai ya bhaagne ki koi tarkeeb hai (He has died because of his own deeds. Because the way the investigation has been going on in the Sushant Singh Rajput and Disha Salian case many are being exposed. Even if there was a connection far off, their names are coming up now. So he can't run away. I am still doubting that he has really died or if this is another of his tricks)."

Notably, Tanushree went on to add, “I will not hesitate to speak the truth because I am not scared.” In a previous post, Tanushree alluded to the abuse she alleged Nana had committed. She re-put up a post written by Sandhya Mridul, which read: “Does a person stop being an abuser when they die? Does the harm they caused disappear too? For survivors, it doesn't.” She also reshared a video recounting how she refused to do an unscripted intimate step with Nana, and was only attacked for it. Tanushree also filed police complaints and with the artist association, but no action was taken.

As per the latest buzz, After news broke of Nana’s death, Tanushree posted videos of her boarding a flight to Lucknow for an event. In a video, she shared, “Maine suna hai, I have heard the news. I just… today is my workday. I am going to Lucknow for an event. And I want to focus on that. What an odd day for all this to happen."

In further updates, She also added, "Because I’m doing a very big event in Lucknow, and it was pretty important for me. I had my entire day planned out. I wanted to do all these Lives and post content. And now I’m worried that in the evening, that’s all the media is going to be interested in is evil dead. So, I will give my reaction once I figure out what kind of reaction I should have. So, definitely condolences to the family but...” and her video cut off midway.

On top of that, Tanushree accused Nana of sexual harassment on the set of the 2009 movie Horn 'Ok' Pleassss. In 2018, during the Me Too movement, the claim became public. An FIR was registered against Nana, who denied the allegations. In 2019, the case was closed for lack of sufficient evidence. In 2025, the Mumbai Andheri Magistrate Court officially dismissed the criminal proceedings against Nana because the complaint was filed beyond the legal limitation period.

title: Imran Khan detained amid police crackdown at August Kranti Maidan protest in Mumbai, posts selfie from police van: ‘Apparently I’m going for a drive’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Imran Khan has been detained by the Mumbai Police on October 10. As per the latest update from news agency ANI, the star was detained from Mumbai's August Kranti Maidan, which was the proposed protest venue in support of CJP’s protest call.

Adding to this, Star Imran Khan has been detained in Mumbai on October 10. (Raju Shinde/HT) The star posted on Instagram and shared a selfie from inside the police van. “Apparently I’m going for a drive,” he shared in the caption.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Imran Khan (@imrankhan)

Notably, Mumbai Police shared no permission had been sought for the protest in support of the CJP . They also shared they could not grant permission, as the Bombay high court’s directions allow protests to be held only at Azad Maidan. However, CJP workers claimed they had emailed the Mumbai Police seeking permission but had received no response.

As per the latest buzz, Nearly 1,500 people have been detained in Delhi in view of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s Jantar Mantar protest today, the police shared. Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, TMC's Mamata Banerjee and AISA's Neha Bora are among those who were detained in the national capital on Saturday.

In further updates, The star had also showed up for a protest march in July. There, Imran was asked by an aspiring star if he had anything to say to actors who believe that art is not political. Responding to the question, Imran shared, "True art is going to have an individual artist point of you embedded within it, and as part of our human nature, we are going to have opinion and perspective that we hold through to ourselves . If you can’t stand by your opinions and if you do not pour your own heart into your art, your art has no value."

On top of that, Imran had also expressed his support for the student protest on social media. He voiced his discontent over the alleged use of lathi-charge against students, saying that the very system meant to protect and support them had already failed them. He wrote, “Something broke in me today. Watching as police gassed and battered student protestors… how could I make sense of this? These students who worked hard, only to be failed by the system. These people who asked to be heard, only to be met with silence. These citizens who stood up to show what matters to them… beaten down and disowned by the establishment."

The star added, “Are these not the children of Mother India? If not them, for whom do we build, and whose future do we claim to protect? Those who demand ‘organisation’ from students protesting education reform, but don’t apply such lofty standards of accountability to established authority; bootlickers, one and all."
